translations.literal: Northern Qi
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi

sentences.zh: 齊武明皇后婁氏，諱昭君，贈司徒內幹之女也。

translations.literal: Qi Wuming Empress Lou, taboo name Zhaojun, was daughter of Inner Director of the Masters of Works Lou, posthumously Minister of State.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wuming Empress Lou, taboo name Zhaojun, was daughter of Inner Director of the Masters of Works Lou, posthumously minister of state.

sentences.zh: 少明悟，強族多娉之，並不肯行。

translations.literal: In youth she was bright and penetrating; powerful clans many betrothed her—she all refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: In youth she was bright and penetrating; powerful clans many betrothed her—she all refused to go.

sentences.zh: 及見神武城上執役，驚曰：「此真吾夫也。

translations.literal: When she saw Shenwu holding tools on the wall, she was startled: "This is truly my husband."
translations.idiomatic: When she saw Shenwu holding tools on the wall, she was startled, "This is truly my husband."

sentences.zh: 」乃使婢通意，又數致私財，使以娉己，父母不得已而許焉。

translations.literal: She had a maid convey her intent, and several times sent private wealth to have him betroth her; her parents had no choice but to consent.
translations.idiomatic: She had a maid convey her intent, and several times sent private wealth to have him betroth her; her parents had no choice but to consent.

sentences.zh: 神武既有澄清之志，傾產以結英豪，密謀秘策，後恆參預。

translations.literal: When Shenwu had the will to clarify the realm, he poured out his estate to bind heroes; secret plots and strategies—she afterward always took part.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu had the will to clarify the realm, he poured out his estate to bind heroes; secret plots and strategies—she afterward always took part.

sentences.zh: 及拜勃海王妃，閫闈之事悉決焉。

translations.literal: When he was made Princess of Bohai, inner-gate affairs were all decided by her.
translations.idiomatic: When he was made Princess of Bohai, inner-gate affairs were all decided by her.

sentences.zh: 後高明嚴斷，雅遵儉約，往來外舍，侍從不過十人。

translations.literal: Later Gaoming was stern and decisive, always following frugality; coming and going to outer quarters, attendants did not exceed ten.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gaoming was stern and decisive, always following frugality; coming and going to outer quarters, attendants did not exceed ten.

sentences.zh: 性寬厚，不妒忌，神武姬侍咸加恩待。

translations.literal: By nature tolerant and not jealous, all Shenwu's concubines she favored and treated.
translations.idiomatic: By nature tolerant and not jealous, all Shenwu's concubines she favored and treated.

sentences.zh: 神武嘗將西討出師，後夜孿生一男一女，左右以危急，請追告神武。

translations.literal: Shenwu once was about to campaign west; that night the empress bore twin boy and girl; attendants because of danger asked to chase and tell Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu once was about to campaign west; that night the empress bore twin boy and girl; attendants because of danger asked to chase and tell Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 後弗聽，曰：「王出統大兵，何得以我故輕離軍幕？

translations.literal: The empress would not listen, saying: "The king goes to command great armies—how can he lightly leave the camp tent for my sake?
translations.idiomatic: The empress would not listen, saying, "The king goes to command great armies—how can he lightly leave the camp tent for my sake?

sentences.zh: 死生命也，來復何為。

translations.literal: Death and life are fate—what use to come back?"
translations.idiomatic: Death and life are fate—what use to come back?"

sentences.zh: 」神武聞之，嗟歎良久。

translations.literal: When Shenwu heard, he sighed long.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu heard, he sighed long.

sentences.zh: 沙苑敗後，侯景屢言請精騎二萬，必能取之。

translations.literal: After defeat at Shawei, Hou Jing repeatedly asked for twenty thousand elite cavalry and was sure he could take them.
translations.idiomatic: After defeat at Shawei, Hou Jing repeatedly asked for twenty thousand elite cavalry and was sure he could take them.

sentences.zh: 神武悅，以告於後。

translations.literal: Shenwu was pleased and told the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu was pleased and told the empress.

sentences.zh: 後曰：「若如其言，豈有還理？

translations.literal: The empress said: "If it were as he says, would there be any return?
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "If it were as he says, would there be any return?

sentences.zh: 得獺失景，亦有何利。

translations.literal: Gain otter, lose Jing—what profit is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Gain otter, lose Jing—what profit is there?"

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: He stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped.

sentences.zh: 神武逼於蠕蠕，欲娶其女而未決。

translations.literal: Shenwu, pressed by Rouran, wished to marry their daughter but had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu, pressed by Rouran, wished to marry their daughter but had not decided.

sentences.zh: 後曰：「國家大計，願不疑也。

translations.literal: The empress said: "For the state's great plan, I hope you will not doubt."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "For the state's great plan, I hope you will not doubt."

sentences.zh: 」及蠕蠕公主至，後避正室處之，神武愧而拜謝焉。

translations.literal: When the Rouran princess arrived, the empress yielded the principal chamber to her; Shenwu was ashamed and bowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran princess arrived, the empress yielded the principal chamber to her; Shenwu was ashamed and bowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 曰：「彼將有覺，願絕勿顧。

translations.literal: She said: "She will notice—please cut off all regard."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "She will notice—please cut off all regard."

sentences.zh: 」慈愛諸子，不異己出，躬自紡績，人賜一袍一褲。

translations.literal: She loved all sons as if her own, personally spinning; each person was given one robe and one pair of trousers.
translations.idiomatic: She loved all sons as if her own, personally spinning; each person was given one robe and one pair of trousers.

sentences.zh: 手縫戎服，以帥左右。

translations.literal: She hand-stitched military dress to lead attendants.
translations.idiomatic: She hand-stitched military dress to lead attendants.

sentences.zh: 弟昭以功名自達，其餘親屬，未嘗為請爵位，每言有材當用，義不以私亂公。

translations.literal: Younger brother Zhao achieved merit and office himself; other kin never asked for ranks—she always said if there was talent it should be used; righteousness does not let private feeling disorder public affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Zhao achieved merit and office himself; other kin never asked for ranks—she always said if there was talent it should be used; righteousness does not let private feeling disorder public affairs.

sentences.zh: 文襄嗣位，進為太妃。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang succeeded, she was advanced to Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang succeeded, she was advanced to grand consort.

sentences.zh: 文宣將受魏禪，後固執不許，帝所以中止。

translations.literal: Wenxuan was about to receive Wei abdication; the empress firmly would not permit—therefore the emperor stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan was about to receive Wei abdication; the empress firmly would not permit—therefore the emperor stopped.

sentences.zh: 天保初，尊為皇太后，宮曰宣訓。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao she was honored Empress Dowager; palace called Xuanyi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao she was honored empress dowager; palace called Xuanyi.

sentences.zh: 濟南即位，尊為太皇太后。

translations.literal: When Jinan took the throne, she was honored Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinan took the throne, she was honored grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 尚書令楊愔等受遺詔輔政，疏忌諸王。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Yin and others received the deathbed edict to assist government and were suspicious of the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Yin and others received the deathbed edict to assist government and were suspicious of the princes.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后密與孝昭及諸大將定策誅之，下令廢立。

translations.literal: Grand Empress Dowager secretly with Xiaozhao and great generals fixed a plan to execute them and issued orders to depose and establish.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Empress Dowager secretly with Xiaozhao and great generals fixed a plan to execute them and issued orders to depose and establish.

sentences.zh: 孝昭即位，復為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao took the throne, she again became Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao took the throne, she again became empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 孝昭崩，太后又下詔立武成帝。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao died, the empress dowager again issued an edict to establish Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao died, the empress dowager again issued an edict to establish Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 大寧二年春，太后寢疾，衣忽自舉，用巫媼言，改姓石氏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daning spring, the empress dowager was ill; clothes suddenly lifted themselves; following a witch's words, she changed surname to Shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daning spring, the empress dowager was ill; clothes suddenly lifted themselves; following a witch's words, she changed surname to Shi.

sentences.zh: 四月辛丑，崩于北宮，時年六十二。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou of the fourth month she died in the North Palace, age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinchou of the fourth month she died in the North Palace, age sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 五月甲申，合葬義平陵。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen of the fifth month she was buried jointly at Yiping Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiashen of the fifth month she was buried jointly at Yiping Tomb.

sentences.zh: 太后凡孕六男二女，皆感夢。

translations.literal: The empress in all bore six sons and two daughters—all from dreams.
translations.idiomatic: The empress in all bore six sons and two daughters—all from dreams.

sentences.zh: 孕文襄則夢一斷龍；

translations.literal: When pregnant with Wenxiang she dreamed of a broken dragon;
translations.idiomatic: When pregnant with Wenxiang she dreamed of a broken dragon;

sentences.zh: 孕文宣則夢大龍，首尾屬天地，張口動目，勢狀驚人；

translations.literal: when pregnant with Wenxuan she dreamed of a great dragon, head and tail joining Heaven and Earth, mouth open and eyes moving, form terrifying;
translations.idiomatic: when pregnant with Wenxuan she dreamed of a great dragon, head and tail joining Heaven and Earth, mouth open and eyes moving, form terrifying;

sentences.zh: 孕孝昭則夢蠕龍於地；

translations.literal: when pregnant with Xiaozhao she dreamed of a writhing dragon on the ground;
translations.idiomatic: when pregnant with Xiaozhao she dreamed of a writhing dragon on the ground;

sentences.zh: 孕武成則夢龍浴於海；

translations.literal: when pregnant with Wucheng she dreamed of a dragon bathing in the sea;
translations.idiomatic: when pregnant with Wucheng she dreamed of a dragon bathing in the sea;

sentences.zh: 孕魏二後，並夢月入懷；

translations.literal: when pregnant with the two Wei empresses, both dreamed the moon entered the bosom;
translations.idiomatic: when pregnant with the two Wei empresses, both dreamed the moon entered the bosom;

sentences.zh: 孕襄城、博陵二王，夢鼠入衣下。

translations.literal: when pregnant with the Princes of Xiangcheng and Boling, dreamed a rat entered under the clothes.
translations.idiomatic: when pregnant with the Princes of Xiangcheng and Boling, dreamed a rat entered under the clothes.

sentences.zh: 後未崩，有童謠曰：「九龍母死不作孝。

translations.literal: Before the empress died, a children's song said: "Nine dragons' mother dies—no mourning made."
translations.idiomatic: Before the empress died, a children's song said, "Nine dragons' mother dies—no mourning made."

sentences.zh: 」及後崩，武成不改服，緋袍如故。

translations.literal: When the empress died, Wucheng did not change dress—crimson robe as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress died, Wucheng did not change dress—crimson robe as before.

sentences.zh: 未幾，登三台，置酒作樂；

translations.literal: Before long he ascended the Three Terraces, set wine and made music;
translations.idiomatic: Before long he ascended the Three Terraces, set wine and made music;

sentences.zh: 宮女進白袍，帝怒，投諸台下。

translations.literal: a palace woman presented a white robe; the emperor was angry and threw it below the terrace.
translations.idiomatic: a palace woman presented a white robe; the emperor was angry and threw it below the terrace.

sentences.zh: 和士開請止樂，帝大怒，撾之。

translations.literal: He Shikai asked to stop the music; the emperor greatly angered and beat him.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai asked to stop the music; the emperor greatly angered and beat him.

sentences.zh: 帝于昆季，次實九，蓋其征驗也。

translations.literal: Among the emperor's brothers he was actually ninth—this was its omen.
translations.idiomatic: Among the emperor's brothers he was actually ninth—this was its omen.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕公主者，蠕蠕主郁久閭阿那瑰女也。

translations.literal: The Rouran princess was daughter of Rouran lord Yujiulü Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran princess was daughter of Rouran lord Yujiulü Anagui.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕強盛，與西魏通和，欲連兵東伐。

translations.literal: Rouran was strong and made peace with Western Wei, wishing to join forces and campaign east.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran was strong and made peace with Western Wei, wishing to join forces and campaign east.

sentences.zh: 神武病之，令杜弼使蠕蠕，為世子求婚。

translations.literal: Shenwu was troubled; he sent Du Bi to Rouran to betroth the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu was troubled; he sent Du Bi to Rouran to betroth the heir.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰曰：「高王自娶則可。

translations.literal: Anagui said: "If High King marries her himself, it may be done."
translations.idiomatic: Anagui said, "If High King marries her himself, it may be done."

sentences.zh: 」神武猶豫，尉景與武明皇后及文襄並勸請，乃從之。

translations.literal: Shenwu hesitated; Wei Jing with Wuming Empress and Wenxiang all urged—then he followed.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu hesitated; Wei Jing with Wuming Empress and Wenxiang all urged—then he followed.

sentences.zh: 武定三年，使慕容儼往娉之，號曰蠕蠕公主。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wuding he sent Murong Yan to betroth her; title Princess Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wuding he sent Murong Yan to betroth her; title Princess Rouran.

sentences.zh: 八月，神武迎於下館，阿那瑰使其弟禿突佳來送女，且報聘，仍戒曰：「待見外孫，然後返國。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Shenwu welcomed her at the lower lodge; Anagui sent his younger brother Tutuqi to escort the girl and return the betrothal gift, also admonishing: "Wait until you see the grandson, then return home."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Shenwu welcomed her at the lower lodge; Anagui sent his younger brother Tutuqi to escort the girl and return the betrothal gift, also admonishing, "Wait until you see the grandson, then return home."

sentences.zh: 」公主性嚴毅，一生不肯華言。

translations.literal: The princess was stern and resolute; all her life she would not speak Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was stern and resolute; all her life she would not speak Chinese.

sentences.zh: 神武嘗有病，不得往公主所，禿突佳怨恚，神武自射堂輿疾就公主。

translations.literal: Shenwu once was ill and could not go to the princess's place; Tutuqi resented it; Shenwu from the archery hall took illness and went to the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu once was ill and could not go to the princess's place; Tutuqi resented it; Shenwu from the archery hall took illness and went to the princess.

sentences.zh: 其見將護如此。

translations.literal: Such was how he was seen to protect her.
translations.idiomatic: Such was how he was seen to protect her.

sentences.zh: 神武崩，文襄從蠕蠕國法，蒸公主，產一女焉。

translations.literal: When Shenwu died, Wenxiang followed Rouran custom and took the princess in union; she bore a daughter.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu died, Wenxiang followed Rouran custom and took the princess in union; she bore a daughter.

sentences.zh: 彭城太妃爾硃氏，榮之女，魏孝莊後也。

translations.literal: Pengcheng Grand Consort Erzhu was Rong's daughter, empress of Wei Xiaozhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Pengcheng Grand Consort Erzhu was Rong's daughter, empress of Wei Xiaozhuang.

sentences.zh: 神武納為別室，敬重逾于婁妃，見必束帶，自稱下官。

translations.literal: Shenwu took her as a separate chamber; respect exceeded Consort Lou; on meeting he always girded his belt and called himself subordinate official.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu took her as a separate chamber; respect exceeded Consort Lou; on meeting he always girded his belt and called himself subordinate official.

sentences.zh: 神武迎蠕蠕公主還，爾硃氏迎于木井北，與蠕蠕公主前後別行，不相見。

translations.literal: When Shenwu welcomed the Rouran princess back, Erzhu met her north of Mujing; with the Rouran princess they traveled one before and one after, not meeting.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu welcomed the Rouran princess back, Erzhu met her north of Mujing; with the Rouran princess they traveled one before and one after, not meeting.

sentences.zh: 公主引角弓仰射翔鴟，應弦而落；

translations.literal: The princess drew a horn bow and shot upward at a soaring hawk—it fell at the bowstring's release;
translations.idiomatic: The princess drew a horn bow and shot upward at a soaring hawk—it fell at the bowstring's release;

sentences.zh: 妃引長弓斜射飛烏，亦一發而中。

translations.literal: the consort drew a long bow and shot obliquely at a flying crow—also one shot and hit.
translations.idiomatic: the consort drew a long bow and shot obliquely at a flying crow—also one shot and hit.

sentences.zh: 神武喜曰：「我此二婦，並堪擊賊。

translations.literal: Shenwu joyfully said: "My two wives are both fit to strike bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu joyfully said, "My two wives are both fit to strike bandits."

sentences.zh: 」後為尼，神武為起佛寺。

translations.literal: Later she became a nun; Shenwu built a Buddhist temple for her.
translations.idiomatic: Later she became a nun; Shenwu built a Buddhist temple for her.

sentences.zh: 天保初，為太妃。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao she was Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao she was grand consort.

sentences.zh: 及文宣狂酒，將無禮於太妃，太妃不從，遂遇禍。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan in mad wine would be without ritual toward the grand consort, she would not yield and met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan in mad wine would be without ritual toward the grand consort, she would not yield and met disaster.

sentences.zh: 小爾硃者，兆之女也。

translations.literal: Young Erzhu was Zhao's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Young Erzhu was Zhao's daughter.

sentences.zh: 初為建明皇后。

translations.literal: At first she was Jianming empress.
translations.idiomatic: At first she was Jianming empress.

sentences.zh: 神武納之，生任城王。

translations.literal: Shenwu took her in; she bore Prince of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu took her in; she bore Prince of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 未幾，與趙郡公琛私通，徙於靈州。

translations.literal: Before long she privately communicated with Duke of Zhao Chen and was moved to Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long she privately communicated with Duke of Zhao Chen and was moved to Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 後適范陽盧景璋。

translations.literal: Later she married Lu Jingzhang of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later she married Lu Jingzhang of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 上党太妃韓氏，軌之妹也。

translations.literal: Shangdang Grand Consort Han was younger sister of Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Shangdang Grand Consort Han was younger sister of Gui.

sentences.zh: 神武微時欲娉之，軌母不許。

translations.literal: When Shenwu was slight in status he wished to betroth her; Gui's mother did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu was slight in status he wished to betroth her; Gui's mother did not permit.

sentences.zh: 及神武貴，韓氏夫已死，乃納之。

translations.literal: When Shenwu was noble, Han's husband had died—then he took her in.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu was noble, Han's husband had died—then he took her in.

sentences.zh: 馮翊太妃鄭氏，名大車，嚴祖妹也。

translations.literal: Fengyi Grand Consort Zheng, name Dache, was younger sister of Yanzu.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyi Grand Consort Zheng, name Dache, was younger sister of Yanzu.

sentences.zh: 初為魏廣平王妃。

translations.literal: At first she was consort of Wei Prince of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: At first she was consort of Wei Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 遷鄴後，神武納之，寵冠後庭，生馮翊王潤。

translations.literal: After moving to Ye, Shenwu took her in; favor topped the rear court; she bore Prince of Fengyi Run.
translations.idiomatic: After moving to Ye, Shenwu took her in; favor topped the rear court; she bore Prince of Fengyi Run.

sentences.zh: 神武之征劉蠡升，文襄蒸於大車。

translations.literal: When Shenwu campaigned against Liu Liesheng, Wenxiang violated Dache.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu campaigned against Liu Liesheng, Wenxiang violated Dache.

sentences.zh: 神武還，一婢告之，二婢為證。

translations.literal: When Shenwu returned, one maid reported it; two maids were witnesses.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu returned, one maid reported it; two maids were witnesses.

sentences.zh: 神武杖文襄一百而幽之，武明後亦見隔絕。

translations.literal: Shenwu beat Wenxiang a hundred strokes and confined him; Wuming Empress was also cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu beat Wenxiang a hundred strokes and confined him; Wuming Empress was also cut off.

sentences.zh: 時彭城爾硃太妃有寵，生王子浟，神武將有廢立意。

translations.literal: At the time Pengcheng Erzhu Grand Consort had favor and bore Prince You; Shenwu had intent to depose.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Pengcheng Erzhu Grand Consort had favor and bore Prince You; Shenwu had intent to depose.

sentences.zh: 文襄求救于司馬子如。

translations.literal: Wenxiang sought rescue from Sima Ziru.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang sought rescue from Sima Ziru.

sentences.zh: 子如來朝，偽為不知者，請武明後。

translations.literal: Ziru came to court, feigning ignorance, and requested Wuming Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru came to court, feigning ignorance, and requested Wuming Empress.

sentences.zh: 神武告其故。

translations.literal: Shenwu told him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu told him the reason.

sentences.zh: 子如曰：「消難亦奸子如妾，如此事，正可覆蓋。

translations.literal: Ziru said: "Xiaonan also violated Ziru's concubine—such matters should simply be covered.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru said, "Xiaonan also violated Ziru's concubine—such matters should simply be covered.

sentences.zh: 妃是王結髮婦，常以父母家財奉王，王在懷朔被杖，背無完皮，妃晝夜供給看瘡。

translations.literal: The consort is the king's hair-bound wife; she always used her parents' house wealth to serve the king; when the king at Huaishuo was beaten, his back had no whole skin—the consort day and night supplied and tended the sores.
translations.idiomatic: The consort is the king's hair-bound wife; she always used her parents' house wealth to serve the king; when the king at Huaishuo was beaten, his back had no whole skin—the consort day and night supplied and tended the sores.

sentences.zh: 後避葛賊，同走并州。

translations.literal: Later avoiding Ge bandits, together fleeing to Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later avoiding Ge bandits, together fleeing to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 貧困，然馬屎，自作靴，恩義何可忘？

translations.literal: In poverty they ate horse dung; she made boots herself—how can such grace be forgotten?
translations.idiomatic: In poverty they ate horse dung; she made boots herself—how can such grace be forgotten?

sentences.zh: 夫婦相宜，女配至尊，男承大業，又婁領軍勳，何宜搖動？

translations.literal: Husband and wife suit each other; the woman matches supreme honor, the man inherits great enterprise—also Lou the commander-in-chief's merit—why should it be shaken?
translations.idiomatic: Husband and wife suit each other; the woman matches supreme honor, the man inherits great enterprise—also Lou the commander-in-chief's merit—why should it be shaken?

sentences.zh: 一女子如草芥，況婢言不必信。

translations.literal: One woman is like grass; moreover the maids' words need not be believed."
translations.idiomatic: One woman is like grass; moreover the maids' words need not be believed."

sentences.zh: 」神武因使子如鞫之。

translations.literal: Shenwu therefore had Ziru interrogate.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu therefore had Ziru interrogate.

sentences.zh: 子如見文襄，尤之曰：「男兒何意畏威自誣？

translations.literal: Ziru saw Wenxiang and reproached him: "What meaning has a man to fear authority and falsely accuse himself?"
translations.idiomatic: Ziru saw Wenxiang and reproached him, "What meaning has a man to fear authority and falsely accuse himself?"

sentences.zh: 」因教二婢反辭，脅告者自縊，乃啟神武曰：「果虛言。

translations.literal: He taught the two maids to reverse their testimony, coerced the accuser to hang herself, then reported to Shenwu: "It was truly empty words."
translations.idiomatic: He taught the two maids to reverse their testimony, coerced the accuser to hang herself, then reported to Shenwu, "It was truly empty words."

sentences.zh: 」神武大悅，召後及文襄。

translations.literal: " Shenwu greatly rejoiced and summoned the empress and Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: " Shenwu greatly rejoiced and summoned the empress and Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 武明後遙見神武，一步一叩頭。

translations.literal: Wuming Empress from afar saw Shenwu—one step one knock of the head.
translations.idiomatic: Wuming Empress from afar saw Shenwu—one step one knock of the head.

sentences.zh: 文襄且拜且進，父子夫妻相泣，乃如初。

translations.literal: Wenxiang both bowed and advanced; father, son, husband and wife wept together—then as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang both bowed and advanced; father, son, husband and wife wept together—then as at first.

sentences.zh: 神武乃置酒曰：「全我父子者，司馬子如。

translations.literal: Shenwu then set wine: "He who preserved me father and son was Sima Ziru."
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu then set wine, "He who preserved me father and son was Sima Ziru."

sentences.zh: 」賜之黃金百三十斤，文襄贈良馬五十匹。

translations.literal: He granted him one hundred thirty jin of yellow gold; Wenxiang gifted fifty fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: He granted him one hundred thirty jin of yellow gold; Wenxiang gifted fifty fine horses.

sentences.zh: 高陽太妃游氏，父京之，為相州長史。

translations.literal: Gaoyang Grand Consort You—father Jingzhi was chief clerk of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyang Grand Consort You—father Jingzhi was chief clerk of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 神武克鄴，欲納之；

translations.literal: When Shenwu took Ye he wished to take her in;
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu took Ye he wished to take her in;

sentences.zh: 京之不許，遂牽曳取之。

translations.literal: Jingzhi did not permit; he was dragged and taken.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhi did not permit; he was dragged and taken.

sentences.zh: 京之尋死。

translations.literal: Jingzhi soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhi soon died.

sentences.zh: 游氏于諸太妃中最有德訓，諸王、公主婚嫁，常令主之。

translations.literal: Among all grand consorts You had most moral instruction; princes' and princesses' marriages and betrothals were often put in her charge.
translations.idiomatic: Among all grand consorts You had most moral instruction; princes' and princesses' marriages and betrothals were often put in her charge.

sentences.zh: 馮娘者，子昂妹也，初為魏任城王妃，適爾硃世隆。

translations.literal: Lady Feng was Zi'ang's younger sister; at first consort of Wei Prince of Rencheng; she married Erzhu Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Feng was Zi'ang's younger sister; at first consort of Wei Prince of Rencheng; she married Erzhu Shilong.

sentences.zh: 神武納之，生浮陽公主。

translations.literal: Shenwu took her in; she bore Princess of Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu took her in; she bore Princess of Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 李娘者，延實從妹也。

translations.literal: Lady Li was Yanshi's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was Yanshi's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 初為魏城陽王妃。

translations.literal: At first consort of Wei Prince of Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: At first consort of Wei Prince of Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 又王娘生永安王浚，穆娘生平陽王淹。

translations.literal: Also Lady Wang bore Prince of Yong'an Jun; Lady Mu bore Prince of Pingyang Yan—both died early and were not grand consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Also Lady Wang bore Prince of Yong'an Jun; Lady Mu bore Prince of Pingyang Yan—both died early and were not grand consorts.

sentences.zh: 並早卒，不為太妃。

translations.literal: Both died early and were not grand consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Both died early and were not grand consorts.

sentences.zh: 文襄敬皇后元氏，魏孝靜帝之姊也。

translations.literal: Wenxiang Jing Empress Yuan was younger sister of Wei Emperor Xiaojing.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang Jing Empress Yuan was younger sister of Wei Emperor Xiaojing.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝時，封馮翊公主，而歸於文襄。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu she was enfeoffed Princess of Fengyi and returned to Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu she was enfeoffed Princess of Fengyi and returned to Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 容德兼美，曲盡和敬。

translations.literal: Bearing and virtue both beautiful; harmony and respect fully achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing and virtue both beautiful; harmony and respect fully achieved.

sentences.zh: 初生河間王孝琬，時文襄為世子，三日而孝靜幸世子第，贈錦彩及布帛萬匹。

translations.literal: First she bore Prince of Hejian Xiaowan; at the time Wenxiang was heir; on the third day Xiaojing visited the heir's residence and gifted ten thousand bolts of brocade and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: First she bore Prince of Hejian Xiaowan; at the time Wenxiang was heir; on the third day Xiaojing visited the heir's residence and gifted ten thousand bolts of brocade and cloth.

sentences.zh: 世子辭，求通受諸貴禮遺，於是十屋皆滿。

translations.literal: The heir declined; he asked to receive together the nobles' ritual gifts—then ten rooms were all full.
translations.idiomatic: The heir declined; he asked to receive together the nobles' ritual gifts—then ten rooms were all full.

sentences.zh: 次生兩公主。

translations.literal: Next she bore two princesses.
translations.idiomatic: Next she bore two princesses.

sentences.zh: 文宣受禪，尊為文襄皇后，居靜德宮。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan received abdication, she was honored Wenxiang Empress and dwelt at Jingde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan received abdication, she was honored Wenxiang Empress and dwelt at Jingde Palace.

sentences.zh: 及天保六年，文宣漸致昏狂，乃移居于高陽之宅而取其府庫，曰：「吾兄昔奸我婦，我今須報。

translations.literal: By the sixth year of Tianbao Wenxuan gradually fell into mad frenzy; he moved her to Gaoyang's residence and took her treasury, saying: "My elder brother once violated my wife—now I must repay."
translations.idiomatic: By the sixth year of Tianbao Wenxuan gradually fell into mad frenzy; he moved her to Gaoyang's residence and took her treasury, saying, "My elder brother once violated my wife—now I must repay."

sentences.zh: 」乃淫於後。

translations.literal: Then he violated the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Then he violated the empress.

sentences.zh: 其高氏女婦，無親疏皆使左右亂交之於前。

translations.literal: Gao women, consorts—without regard for near or far—all he had attendants disorderly join them before him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao women, consorts—without regard for near or far—all he had attendants disorderly join them before him.

sentences.zh: 以葛為絙，令魏安德主騎上，使人推引之。

translations.literal: With hemp as a rope he ordered Princess of Wei Ande ride atop; men pushed and drew her.
translations.idiomatic: With hemp as a rope he ordered Princess of Wei Ande ride atop; men pushed and drew her.

sentences.zh: 又命胡人苦辱之。

translations.literal: Also he ordered barbarians cruelly to humiliate them.
translations.idiomatic: Also he ordered barbarians cruelly to humiliate them.

sentences.zh: 帝又自呈露，以示群下。

translations.literal: The emperor also exposed himself to show the crowd below.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also exposed himself to show the crowd below.

sentences.zh: 武平中，後崩，祔葬義平陵。

translations.literal: Under Wuping the empress died and was attached-buried at Yiping Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wuping the empress died and was attached-buried at Yiping Tomb.

sentences.zh: 琅邪公主名玉儀，魏高陽王斌庶生妹也。

translations.literal: Princess of Langye, name Yuyi, was younger uterine sister of Wei Prince of Gaoyang Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Langye, name Yuyi, was younger uterine sister of Wei Prince of Gaoyang Bin.

sentences.zh: 初不見齒，為孫騰妓，騰又放棄。

translations.literal: At first her teeth were not seen; she was Sun Teng's courtesan; Teng again abandoned her.
translations.idiomatic: At first her teeth were not seen; she was Sun Teng's courtesan; Teng again abandoned her.

sentences.zh: 文襄遇諸途，悅而納之，遂被殊寵，奏魏帝封焉。

translations.literal: Wenxiang met her on the road, delighted and took her in; she received exceptional favor; he memorialized the Wei emperor to enfeoff her.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang met her on the road, delighted and took her in; she received exceptional favor; he memorialized the Wei emperor to enfeoff her.

sentences.zh: 文襄謂崔季舒曰：「爾由來為我求色，不如我自得一絕異者。

translations.literal: Wenxiang told Cui Jishu: "You always sought beauty for me—not as good as my finding one utterly unique.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang told Cui Jishu, "You always sought beauty for me—not as good as my finding one utterly unique.

sentences.zh: 崔暹必當造直諫，我亦有以待之。

translations.literal: Cui Kui will surely come with straight remonstrance—I also have means to wait for him."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kui will surely come with straight remonstrance—I also have means to wait for him."

sentences.zh: 」及暹諮事，文襄不復假以顏色。

translations.literal: When Kui reported affairs, Wenxiang no longer lent him a pleasant face.
translations.idiomatic: When Kui reported affairs, Wenxiang no longer lent him a pleasant face.

sentences.zh: 居三日，暹懷刺，墜之於前。

translations.literal: After three days Kui carried a memorial and dropped it before him.
translations.idiomatic: After three days Kui carried a memorial and dropped it before him.

sentences.zh: 文襄問：「何用此為？

translations.literal: Wenxiang asked: "What use is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang asked, "What use is this?"

sentences.zh: 」暹悚然曰：「未得通公主。

translations.literal: Kui fearfully said: "I have not yet obtained access to the princess."
translations.idiomatic: Kui fearfully said, "I have not yet obtained access to the princess."

sentences.zh: 」文襄大悅，把暹臂入見焉。

translations.literal: Wenxiang greatly rejoiced, took Kui's arm and entered to see her.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang greatly rejoiced, took Kui's arm and entered to see her.

sentences.zh: 季舒語人曰：「崔暹常忿吾佞，在大將軍前，每言叔父合殺。

translations.literal: Jishu told others: "Cui Kui always resented my flattery; before the grand marshal he always said my uncle ought to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu told others, "Cui Kui always resented my flattery; before the grand marshal he always said my uncle ought to be killed.

sentences.zh: 及自作體佞，乃體過於吾。

translations.literal: When he himself played the flatterer, his body exceeded mine."
translations.idiomatic: When he himself played the flatterer, his body exceeded mine."

sentences.zh: 」玉儀同產姊靜儀，先適黃門郎崔括，文襄亦幸之，皆封公主。

translations.literal: Yuyi's uterine elder sister Jingyi had first married Attendant-in-Chief Cui Kuo; Wenxiang also favored her—both were enfeoffed princess.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyi's uterine elder sister Jingyi had first married Attendant-in-Chief Cui Kuo; Wenxiang also favored her—both were enfeoffed princess.

sentences.zh: 括父子由是超授，賞賜甚厚焉。

translations.literal: Kuo father and son thereby received extraordinary promotion; rewards were very thick.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo father and son thereby received extraordinary promotion; rewards were very thick.

sentences.zh: 文宣皇后李氏諱祖娥，趙郡李希宗女也。

translations.literal: Wenxuan Empress Li, taboo name Zue, was daughter of Li Xizong of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan Empress Li, taboo name Zue, was daughter of Li Xizong of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 容德甚美。

translations.literal: Bearing and virtue were very beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing and virtue were very beautiful.

sentences.zh: 初為太其原公夫人。

translations.literal: At first she was consort of Duke of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At first she was consort of Duke of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 及帝將建中宮。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to establish the central palace,
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to establish the central palace,

sentences.zh: 高隆之、高德正言漢婦人不可為天下母，宜更擇美配。

translations.literal: Gao Longzhi and Gao Dezheng said Han women could not be mother of the realm—one should again choose a beautiful match.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Longzhi and Gao Dezheng said Han women could not be mother of the realm—one should again choose a beautiful match.

sentences.zh: 楊愔固請依漢、魏故事，不改元妃。

translations.literal: Yang Yin firmly requested following Han and Wei precedent, not changing the original consort.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin firmly requested following Han and Wei precedent, not changing the original consort.

sentences.zh: 而德正猶固請廢後而立段昭儀，欲以結勳貴之援。

translations.literal: Dezheng still firmly requested deposing the empress and establishing Duan zhaoyi, wishing to bind merit-nobles' support.
translations.idiomatic: Dezheng still firmly requested deposing the empress and establishing Duan zhaoyi, wishing to bind merit-nobles' support.

sentences.zh: 帝竟不從而立後焉。

translations.literal: The emperor ultimately did not follow and established the empress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ultimately did not follow and established the empress.

sentences.zh: 帝好捶撻嬪御，乃至有殺戮者，唯後獨家禮敬。

translations.literal: The emperor liked beating pin and attendants—even to killing; only toward the empress alone was ritual respect kept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor liked beating pin and attendants—even to killing; only toward the empress alone was ritual respect kept.

sentences.zh: 天保十年，改為可賀敦皇后。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianbao she was changed to Kehedun Empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tianbao she was changed to Kehedun Empress.

sentences.zh: 孝昭即位，降居昭信宮，號昭信皇后。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao took the throne, she was demoted to Zhaoxin Palace, title Zhaoxin Empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao took the throne, she was demoted to Zhaoxin Palace, title Zhaoxin Empress.

sentences.zh: 武成踐阼，逼後淫亂云：「若不許我，當殺爾兒。

translations.literal: When Wucheng took the throne, he forced the empress into disorder, saying: "If you do not permit me, I will kill your son."
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng took the throne, he forced the empress into disorder, saying, "If you do not permit me, I will kill your son."

sentences.zh: 」後懼，從之。

translations.literal: The empress feared and yielded.
translations.idiomatic: The empress feared and yielded.

sentences.zh: 後有娠，太原王紹德至閣，不得見。

translations.literal: Later she was pregnant; Prince of Taiyuan Shaode came to the pavilion and could not see her.
translations.idiomatic: Later she was pregnant; Prince of Taiyuan Shaode came to the pavilion and could not see her.

sentences.zh: 慍曰：「兒豈不知邪？

translations.literal: Angrily he said: "Does the child not know?
translations.idiomatic: Angrily he said, "Does the child not know?

sentences.zh: 姊姊腹大，故不見兒。

translations.literal: Elder sister's belly is big—therefore she does not see the child."
translations.idiomatic: Elder sister's belly is big—therefore she does not see the child."

sentences.zh: 」後聞之大慚，由是生女不舉。

translations.literal: When the empress heard she was greatly ashamed; from this she bore girls and did not raise them.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress heard she was greatly ashamed; from this she bore girls and did not raise them.

sentences.zh: 帝橫刀詬曰：「爾殺我女，我何不殺爾兒？

translations.literal: The emperor with a bare blade cursed: "You killed my daughter—why should I not kill your son?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor with a bare blade cursed, "You killed my daughter—why should I not kill your son?"

sentences.zh: 」對後前築殺紹德。

translations.literal: Before the empress he built and killed Shaode.
translations.idiomatic: Before the empress he built and killed Shaode.

sentences.zh: 後大哭，帝愈怒，裸後亂撾撻之，號天不已。

translations.literal: The empress wept greatly; the emperor grew angrier, stripped the empress and beat her disorderly; she cried to Heaven without end.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wept greatly; the emperor grew angrier, stripped the empress and beat her disorderly; she cried to Heaven without end.

sentences.zh: 盛以絹囊，流血淋漉，投諸渠水，良久乃蘇，犢車載送妙勝尼寺。

translations.literal: He packed her in a silk bag; blood dripped soaking; he cast her into the canal water; after long while she revived; an ox-cart carried her to Miaosheng Nunnery.
translations.idiomatic: He packed her in a silk bag; blood dripped soaking; he cast her into the canal water; after a long while she revived; an ox-cart carried her to Miaosheng Nunnery.

sentences.zh: 後性愛佛法，因此為尼。

translations.literal: The empress by nature loved Buddhist law; therefore she became a nun.
translations.idiomatic: The empress by nature loved Buddhist law; therefore she became a nun.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，入關，隋時得還趙郡。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, she entered Guanzhong; under Sui she could return to Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell, she entered Guanzhong; under Sui she could return to Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 段昭儀，韶妹也。

translations.literal: Duan zhaoyi was Shao's younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: Duan zhaoyi was Shao's younger sister.

sentences.zh: 婚夕，韶妻元氏為俗弄女婿法戲文宣，文宣銜之。

translations.literal: On the wedding evening Shao's wife Lady Yuan performed vulgar teasing of the son-in-law for Wenxuan; Wenxuan harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: On the wedding evening Shao's wife Lady Yuan performed vulgar teasing of the son-in-law for Wenxuan; Wenxuan harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 後因發怒，謂韶曰：「我會殺爾婦！

translations.literal: Later because of anger he told Shao: "I will kill your wife!"
translations.idiomatic: Later because of anger he told Shao, "I will kill your wife!"

sentences.zh: 」元氏懼，匿婁太后家，終文宣世不敢出。

translations.literal: Lady Yuan feared and hid at Empress Dowager Lou's house; through Wenxuan's age she dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yuan feared and hid at Empress Dowager Lou's house; through Wenxuan's age she dared not come out.

sentences.zh: 昭儀才色兼美，禮遇殆同正嫡。

translations.literal: Zhaoyi had talent and beauty together; courtesy nearly equaled the principal wife.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyi had talent and beauty together; courtesy nearly equaled the principal wife.

sentences.zh: 後主時，改適錄尚書唐邕。

translations.literal: Under the later lord she remarried Director of Records Tang Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Under the later lord she remarried Director of Records Tang Yong.

sentences.zh: 王嬪者，琅邪人也。

translations.literal: Lady Wang pin was a man of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang pin was a man of Langye.

sentences.zh: 嬪姊先適崔修，文宣並幸之。

translations.literal: The pin's elder sister had first married Cui Xiu; Wenxuan favored both.
translations.idiomatic: The pin's elder sister had first married Cui Xiu; Wenxuan favored both.

sentences.zh: 數數降其夫家，超用修為尚書郎。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he lowered himself to their husband's house and promoted Xiu to Masters of Writing lang.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly he lowered himself to their husband's house and promoted Xiu to Masters of Writing lang.

sentences.zh: 薛嬪者，本倡家女也。

translations.literal: Lady Xue pin was originally a singing-house girl.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xue pin was originally a singing-house girl.

sentences.zh: 年十四五時，為清河王嶽所好。

translations.literal: At fourteen or fifteen she was liked by Prince of Qinghe Yue.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen or fifteen she was liked by Prince of Qinghe Yue.

sentences.zh: 其父求內宮中，大被嬖寵。

translations.literal: Her father asked to enter the inner palace; she was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: Her father asked to enter the inner palace; she was greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 其姊亦俱進禦。

translations.literal: Her elder sister also both entered to attend.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder sister also both entered to attend.

sentences.zh: 文宣後知先與嶽通，又為其父乞司徒公。

translations.literal: Later Wenxuan learned she had earlier communicated with Yue; also her father begged Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wenxuan learned she had earlier communicated with Yue; also her father begged Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，先鋸殺其姊。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly angered; first he sawed and killed her elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly angered; first he sawed and killed her elder sister.

sentences.zh: 薛嬪當時有娠，過產亦從戮。

translations.literal: Lady Xue pin was then pregnant; at delivery she was also executed with the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xue pin was then pregnant; at delivery she was also executed with the rest.

sentences.zh: 武成皇后胡氏，安定胡延之女。

translations.literal: Wucheng Empress Hu was daughter of Hu Yan of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng Empress Hu was daughter of Hu Yan of Anding.

sentences.zh: 其母范陽盧道約女。

translations.literal: Her mother was daughter of Fanyang Lu Daoyue.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was daughter of Fanyang Lu Daoyue.

sentences.zh: 初懷孕，有胡僧詣門曰：「此宅瓠蘆中有月。

translations.literal: At first pregnancy a Hu monk came to the door saying: "In this house's bottle-gourd is a moon."
translations.idiomatic: At first pregnancy a Hu monk came to the door saying, "In this house's bottle-gourd is a moon."

sentences.zh: 」既而生後。

translations.literal: Then the empress was born.
translations.idiomatic: Then the empress was born.

sentences.zh: 天保初，選為長廣王妃。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao she was chosen as Prince of Changgung's consort.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao she was chosen as Prince of Changgung's consort.

sentences.zh: 產後主日，有鴞鳴於產帳上。

translations.literal: On the day the later lord was born, an owl cried on the birth canopy.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the later lord was born, an owl cried on the birth canopy.

sentences.zh: 武成崩，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Wucheng died she was honored Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng died she was honored empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 陸媼及和士開密謀殺趙郡王睿，出婁定遠、高文遙為刺史。

translations.literal: Lu the wet-nurse and He Shikai secretly plotted to kill Prince of Zhao Chen; they sent out Lou Dingyuan and Gao Wenyao as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Lu the wet-nurse and He Shikai secretly plotted to kill Prince of Zhao Chen; they sent out Lou Dingyuan and Gao Wenyao as prefects.

sentences.zh: 和、陸諂事太后，無所不至。

translations.literal: He and Lu fawned on the empress dowager to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He and Lu fawned on the empress dowager to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 初，武成時，後與諸閹人褻狎。

translations.literal: At first under Wucheng the empress had indecent dealings with various eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: At first under Wucheng the empress had indecent dealings with various eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 武成寵倖和士開。

translations.literal: Wucheng favored He Shikai.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng favored He Shikai.

sentences.zh: 每與後握槊，因此與後奸通。

translations.literal: Each time with the empress he played spear-game—thereby he communicated in adultery with the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Each time with the empress he played spear-game—thereby he communicated in adultery with the empress.

sentences.zh: 自武成崩後，數出詣佛寺，又與沙門曇獻通。

translations.literal: From after Wucheng's death she often went out to Buddhist temples; also she communicated with the monk Tanxian.
translations.idiomatic: From after Wucheng's death she often went out to Buddhist temples; also she communicated with the monk Tanxian.

sentences.zh: 布金錢於獻度下，又掛寶裝胡床於獻屋壁，武成平生之所禦也。

translations.literal: She spread gold money under Tanxian's ordination platform; also hung a treasure-adorned Hu bed on Tanxian's room wall—what Wucheng in life had used.
translations.idiomatic: She spread gold money under Tanxian's ordination platform; also hung a treasure-adorned Hu bed on Tanxian's room wall—what Wucheng in life had used.

sentences.zh: 乃置百僧於內殿，托以聽講，日夜與曇獻寢處。

translations.literal: Then she placed a hundred monks in the inner hall, under pretext of hearing lectures—day and night she slept with Tanxian.
translations.idiomatic: Then she placed a hundred monks in the inner hall, under pretext of hearing lectures—day and night she slept with Tanxian.

sentences.zh: 以獻為昭玄統。

translations.literal: She made Tanxian Director of Illuminated Mystery.
translations.idiomatic: She made Tanxian Director of Illuminated Mystery.

sentences.zh: 僧徒遙指太后以弄曇獻，乃至謂之為太上者。

translations.literal: Monks from afar pointed at the empress dowager to tease Tanxian—even calling her the Supreme One.
translations.idiomatic: Monks from afar pointed at the empress dowager to tease Tanxian—even calling her the Supreme One.

sentences.zh: 帝聞太后不謹，而未之信。

translations.literal: The emperor heard the empress dowager was improper, but did not yet believe it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had heard the empress dowager was behaving improperly, but did not yet believe it.

sentences.zh: 後朝太后，見二少尼，悅而召之，乃男子也。

translations.literal: Later when he attended the empress dowager, he saw two young nuns, took pleasure in them and summoned them — they were men.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he went to attend the empress dowager, he saw two young nuns, took a liking to them, and summoned them — only to find they were men in disguise.

sentences.zh: 於是曇獻事亦發，皆伏法。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Tanxian affair also broke; all were executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the affair with the monk Tanxian also came to light; all involved were executed.

sentences.zh: 並殺元山王三郡君，皆太后之所昵也。

translations.literal: Together they also killed the three commandery ladies of Prince of Yuanshan, all whom the empress dowager had been intimate with.
translations.idiomatic: They also executed the three commandery ladies of the Prince of Yuanshan, all favorites of the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 帝自晉陽奉太后還鄴，至紫陌，卒遇大風。

translations.literal: The emperor from Jinyang escorted the empress dowager back to Ye; at Zimo they suddenly met a great wind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor escorted the empress dowager back from Jinyang to Ye; at Zimo they were suddenly struck by a violent wind.

sentences.zh: 兼舍人魏僧伽明風角。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary Wei Sengqia understood wind angles.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant-in-ordinary Wei Sengqia was skilled in reading omens from the wind.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「即時當有暴逆事。

translations.literal: He memorialized saying: "At this moment there will be violent treason.
translations.idiomatic: He reported, "At this very moment there will be violent treason.

sentences.zh: 」帝詐云鄴中有急，彎弓纏弰，馳入南城。

translations.literal: " The emperor falsely said there was an emergency in Ye, bent his bow and wound the string, and galloped into the Southern City.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor pretended there was an emergency in Ye, strung his bow, and galloped into the Southern City.

sentences.zh: 令鄧長顒幽太后北宮。

translations.literal: He ordered Deng Changyan to imprison the empress dowager in the Northern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Deng Changyan to confine the empress dowager in the Northern Palace.

sentences.zh: 仍有敕，內外諸親一不得與太后相見。

translations.literal: There was still an edict: inside and outside, all kin were forbidden to see the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed forbidding all relatives, inside and outside the palace, from seeing the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝迎復太后。

translations.literal: After a long time the emperor welcomed the empress dowager back.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the emperor brought the empress dowager back.

sentences.zh: 太后初聞使者至，大驚，慮有不測。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager first heard envoys had come, she was greatly alarmed, fearing the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager first heard that envoys had arrived, she was terrified, fearing the worst.

sentences.zh: 每太后設食，帝亦不敢嘗。

translations.literal: Whenever the empress dowager set out food, the emperor also did not dare taste it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the empress dowager prepared food, the emperor would not dare to taste it.

sentences.zh: 周使元偉來聘，作《述行賦》，敘鄭莊公克段而遷薑氏。

translations.literal: A Zhou envoy Yuan Wei came on a mission of courtesy and composed the Narrative of a Journey, recounting Duke Zhuang of Zheng's overcoming of Duan and removal of Lady Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: A Zhou envoy, Yuan Wei, came on a diplomatic visit and composed the Narrative of a Journey, recounting how Duke Zhuang of Zheng overcame his brother Duan and banished their mother Lady Jiang.

sentences.zh: 文雖不工，當時深以為愧。

translations.literal: Though the writing was not skilled, at the time they were deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Though the piece was not well written, at the time it caused deep shame.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，入周，恣行奸穢。

translations.literal: When Qi perished he entered Zhou and indulged in lewd wickedness without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi fell he entered Northern Zhou and gave himself over to lewd and wicked conduct.

sentences.zh: 開皇中殂。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Kaihuang reign.

sentences.zh: 弘德夫人李氏，趙郡李叔讓女也。

translations.literal: Lady of Manifest Virtue Li was the daughter of Li Shurang of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Manifest Virtue, surnamed Li, was the daughter of Li Shurang of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 初為魏靜帝嬪，武成納焉。

translations.literal: At first she was a consort of Emperor Jing of Wei; Wucheng took her in.
translations.idiomatic: She had first been a consort of Emperor Jing of Wei; Wucheng took her into the palace.

sentences.zh: 生南陽王仁盛，為太妃。

translations.literal: She bore Prince of Nanyang Rensheng and became grand consort.
translations.idiomatic: She bore the Prince of Nanyang, Rensheng, and was made grand consort.

sentences.zh: 姊為南安王思妃，坐夫反，以燒死。

translations.literal: Her elder sister was consort to Prince of Nan'an Si; for her husband's rebellion she was burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder sister had been consort to the Prince of Nan'an, Si; when he rebelled she was burned alive.

sentences.zh: 太妃聞之，發狂而薨。

translations.literal: The grand consort heard of it, went mad, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the grand consort heard of it she went mad and died.

sentences.zh: 文宣王嬪及中人盧勒叉妹，武成並以為嬪。

translations.literal: Wenzuan's consort and the younger sister of the inner attendant Lu Lecha — Wucheng took both as consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzuan's consort and the younger sister of the inner attendant Lu Lecha — Wucheng took both as his consorts.

sentences.zh: 武成崩後，胡後令二嬪自殺。

translations.literal: After Wucheng's death the Hu empress ordered the two consorts to kill themselves.
translations.idiomatic: After Wucheng died, Empress Hu ordered the two consorts to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 二嬪悲哭，後主為之惻愴。

translations.literal: The two consorts wept in grief; the later lord was moved to compassion for them.
translations.idiomatic: The two consorts wept bitterly; the later lord was moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 私遺衣物，令出外避焉。

translations.literal: Privately he sent them clothing and had them go outside to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent them clothing and let them leave the palace to escape.

sentences.zh: 盧養淮南王，後為太妃。

translations.literal: Lu raised the Prince of Huainan and later became grand consort.
translations.idiomatic: Lu raised the Prince of Huainan and later became grand consort.

sentences.zh: 又有馬嬪，亦得幸，為後所妒，自縊死。

translations.literal: There was also Consort Ma, who also won favor; the empress was jealous and she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Consort Ma, who likewise won favor; the empress, jealous, drove her to hang herself.

sentences.zh: 彭榮、任祥並有女，因坐父兄事，皆入宮，為文宣所幸。

translations.literal: Peng Rong and Ren Xiang both had daughters; because of their fathers' and brothers' cases they all entered the palace and were favored by Wenzuan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Rong and Ren Xiang each had daughters who, implicated in their fathers' and brothers' crimes, were sent into the palace and favored by Wenzuan.

sentences.zh: 武成以彭為夫人，養齊安王，任生丹楊王，並為太妃。

translations.literal: Wucheng made Peng a lady and raised Prince of Qi'an; Ren bore Prince of Danyang — both became grand consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng made Peng a lady and had her raise the Prince of Qi'an; Ren bore the Prince of Danyang — both were made grand consorts.

sentences.zh: 後主皇后斛律氏，左丞相光之女也。

translations.literal: The later lord's empress Hulu was the daughter of Left Chancellor Guang.
translations.idiomatic: The later lord's empress, surnamed Hulu, was the daughter of the Left Chancellor Guang.

sentences.zh: 初為皇太子妃，後主受禪，立為皇后。

translations.literal: At first she was the crown prince's consort; when the later lord received the abdication she was established empress.
translations.idiomatic: She had first been crown princess; when the later lord succeeded to the throne she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 武平三年正月，生女。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Wuping she bore a daughter.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Wuping she gave birth to a daughter.

sentences.zh: 帝欲悅光，詐稱生男，為之大赦。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to please Guang and falsely claimed a son had been born; for this he proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to please Guang and falsely announced that a son had been born; a great amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 光誅，後廢在別宮，後令為尼。

translations.literal: When Guang was executed the empress was deposed to a separate palace; later she was ordered to become a nun.
translations.idiomatic: After Guang was executed the empress was deposed to a separate palace and later ordered to become a nun.

sentences.zh: 齊滅，嫁為開府元仁妻。

translations.literal: When Qi perished she was married as wife to Yuan Ren, opening the government.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell she was married to Yuan Ren, a commander of the opening-the-government rank.

sentences.zh: 後主皇后胡氏，隴東王長仁女也。

translations.literal: The later lord's empress Hu was the daughter of Prince of Longdong Changren.
translations.idiomatic: The later lord's empress, surnamed Hu, was the daughter of the Prince of Longdong, Changren.

sentences.zh: 胡太后失母儀之道，深以為愧，欲求悅後主，故飾後於宮中。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Hu had lost the way of a mother's propriety and was deeply ashamed; she wished to please the later lord, so she adorned the empress within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu, having failed in maternal propriety, was deeply ashamed and wished to please the later lord, so she had the empress dressed and adorned within the palace.

sentences.zh: 令帝見之。

translations.literal: She had the emperor see her.
translations.idiomatic: She arranged for the emperor to see her.

sentences.zh: 帝果悅，立為弘德夫人，進左昭儀，大被寵愛。

translations.literal: The emperor was indeed pleased; she was established Lady of Manifest Virtue, advanced to Left Zhaoyi, and greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was indeed pleased; she was made Lady of Manifest Virtue, promoted to Left Zhaoyi, and greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 斛律後廢，陸媼欲以穆夫人代之，太后不許。

translations.literal: When Empress Hulu was deposed, Lady Lu wished to replace her with Lady Mu; the empress dowager did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Hulu was deposed, Lady Lu wanted Lady Mu to replace her; the empress dowager refused.

sentences.zh: 祖孝征請立胡昭儀，遂登為皇后。

translations.literal: Zu Xiaozheng requested establishing Hu Zhaoyi; she then ascended as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Xiaozheng urged that Hu Zhaoyi be made empress, and she was duly elevated.

sentences.zh: 陸媼既非勸立，又意在穆夫人，其後于太后前作色而言曰：「何物親侄女，作如此語言！

translations.literal: Lady Lu had not urged the establishment and also had her heart set on Lady Mu; afterward before the empress dowager she made a face and said: "What kind of close niece is this, to speak such words!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Lu had not supported the elevation and still favored Lady Mu; later, before the empress dowager, she scowled and said, "What sort of close niece is this, to speak such words!

sentences.zh: 」太后問有何言。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager asked what words.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager asked what she had said.

sentences.zh: 曰：「不可道。

translations.literal: She said: "Cannot be spoken.
translations.idiomatic: She replied, "It cannot be repeated.

sentences.zh: 」固問之，乃曰：「語大家雲，太后行多非法，不可以訓。

translations.literal: " Pressed repeatedly, she then said: "She told everyone that the empress dowager's conduct is largely unlawful and cannot be taken as instruction.
translations.idiomatic: " Pressed again and again, she finally said, "She told everyone that the empress dowager's conduct is largely unlawful and cannot serve as a model.

sentences.zh: 」太后大怒，喚後出，立剃其發，送令還家。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager was greatly angered, summoned the empress out, had her head shaved, and sent her back home.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager flew into a rage, had the empress brought out, shaved her head, and sent her home.

sentences.zh: 帝思之，每致詩以通意。

translations.literal: The emperor missed her and often sent poems to convey his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor longed for her and often sent poems to express his feelings.

sentences.zh: 後與斛律廢後俱召入內。

translations.literal: Later she and the deposed Empress Hulu were both summoned within.
translations.idiomatic: Later she and the deposed Empress Hulu were both summoned back into the palace.

sentences.zh: 數日而鄴不守，後亦改嫁云。

translations.literal: Within days Ye was not held; the empress also remarried, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Ye fell; the empress is said to have remarried as well.

sentences.zh: 後主皇后穆氏，名邪利，本斛律後從婢也。

translations.literal: The later lord's empress Mu, named Xieli, was originally a attendant maid of Empress Hulu.
translations.idiomatic: The later lord's empress Mu, named Xieli, had originally been a attendant maid of Empress Hulu.

sentences.zh: 母名輕霄，本穆子倫婢也，轉入侍中宋欽道家，奸私而生後，莫知氏族，或云後即欽道女子也。

translations.literal: Her mother was named Qingxiao, originally a maid of Muzilun; she passed into the household of Attendant-in-ordinary Song Qindao, and through illicit relations bore the empress — her clan was unknown; some say the empress was Song Qindao's own daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Qingxiao had been a maid of Muzilun, then entered the household of the attendant-in-ordinary Song Qindao; an illicit affair produced the future empress, whose lineage was unknown — some said she was Song Qindao's own daughter.

sentences.zh: 小字黃花，後字舍利。

translations.literal: Her childhood name was Yellow Flower; her later name was Sheli.
translations.idiomatic: Her childhood name was Yellow Flower; her formal name was Sheli.

sentences.zh: 欽道婦妒，輕霄面黥為宋字。

translations.literal: Song Qindao's wife was jealous; Qingxiao's face was tattooed with the character Song.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qindao's wife was jealous; Qingxiao's face was branded with the character for Song.

sentences.zh: 欽道伏誅，黃花因此故宮。

translations.literal: When Song Qindao was executed, Yellow Flower for this reason entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Qindao was executed, Yellow Flower entered the palace for that reason.

sentences.zh: 有幸于後主，宮內稱為「舍利大監」。

translations.literal: She won favor from the later lord; within the palace she was called "Grand Supervisor Sheli."
translations.idiomatic: She won the later lord's favor; within the palace she was called "Grand Supervisor Sheli."

sentences.zh: 女侍中陸太姬知其寵，養以為女，薦為弘德夫人。

translations.literal: Female attendant-in-ordinary Lady Lu the Great Matriarch knew of her favor and raised her as a daughter, recommending her as Lady of Manifest Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The female attendant-in-ordinary Lady Lu the Great Matriarch, knowing of her favor, adopted her as a daughter and recommended her as Lady of Manifest Virtue.

sentences.zh: 武平元年六月，生皇子恆。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Wuping she bore the prince Heng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of Wuping she bore the prince Heng.

sentences.zh: 于時後主未有儲嗣，陸陰結待，以臣撫之任不可無主。

translations.literal: At that time the later lord had no heir; Lu secretly cultivated favor, saying the task of nurturing by a subject could not be without a master.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the later lord had no heir; Lu cultivated favor in secret, arguing that the duty of raising the child by a subject required a recognized master.

sentences.zh: 時皇后斛律氏，丞相光之女也，慮其懷恨，先令母養之立為皇太子。

translations.literal: Then Empress Hulu, the chancellor Guang's daughter, feared her resentment and first had the mother raise him and establish him crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Hulu, daughter of Chancellor Guang, fearing resentment, first had the mother raise the child and had him named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 陸以國姓之重，穆、陸相對，又奏賜姓穆氏。

translations.literal: Lu, because the state's surname was weighty and Mu and Lu faced each other, also memorialized granting the surname Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, because the imperial surname carried great weight and the names Mu and Lu paired well, also petitioned that the surname Mu be granted.

sentences.zh: 胡庶人之廢也，陸有助焉。

translations.literal: When the Hu commoner was deposed, Lu had helped.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hu consort was deposed, Lu had assisted.

sentences.zh: 故遂立為皇后，大赦。

translations.literal: Therefore she was then established empress; a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore she was established empress and a great amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 初，有折沖將軍元正烈，於鄴城東水中得璽以獻，文曰「天皇后璽」，蓋石氏所作。

translations.literal: Earlier, Quelling-Insurgency General Yuan Zhenglie in the eastern waters of Ye city obtained a seal and presented it; the inscription read "Heavenly Empress Seal" — probably made by the Shi clan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Quelling-Insurgency General Yuan Zhenglie had found a seal in the eastern waters of Ye and presented it; the inscription read "Heavenly Empress Seal," probably a relic of the Shi clan.

sentences.zh: 詔書頒告，以為穆後之瑞焉。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to announce it, taking it as an omen for Empress Mu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed it far and wide, treating it as a portent for Empress Mu.

sentences.zh: 武成為胡後造真珠裙褲，所費不可稱計，被火燒。

translations.literal: Wucheng for Empress Hu made pearl skirt-trousers; the cost was beyond reckoning; they were burned in a fire.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng had pearl skirt-trousers made for Empress Hu at incalculable cost; they were destroyed in a fire.

sentences.zh: 後主既立穆皇后，復為營之。

translations.literal: After the later lord established Empress Mu, he again had them made for her.
translations.idiomatic: After the later lord made Empress Mu, he had them made again for her.

sentences.zh: 屬周武遭太后喪，詔侍中薛孤、康買等為吊使，又遣商胡齎錦彩三萬疋與吊使同往。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Wu of Zhou suffered the empress dowager's mourning; he ordered Attendant-in-ordinary Xue Gu, Kang Mai, and others as condolence envoys, and also sent merchant Hu with thirty thousand bolts of brocade and silk together with the condolence envoys.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Emperor Wu of Zhou was in mourning for his empress dowager; he sent the attendant-in-ordinary Xue Gu, Kang Mai, and others as condolence envoys, and also dispatched a merchant Hu with thirty thousand bolts of brocade and silk to accompany them.

sentences.zh: 欲市真珠，為皇后造七寶車。

translations.literal: They wished to buy pearls to make a seven-jewel carriage for the empress.
translations.idiomatic: They intended to buy pearls to build a seven-jewel carriage for the empress.

sentences.zh: 周人不與交易，然而竟造焉。

translations.literal: The Zhou people would not trade; yet in the end it was made.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou would not sell; nevertheless the carriage was built in the end.

sentences.zh: 先是，童謠曰：「黃花勢欲落，清觴滿杯酌。

translations.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme said: "Yellow Flower's force is about to fall; clear goblets fill the cup and pour.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a children's rhyme had run, "Yellow Flower's force is about to fall; clear goblets fill to the brim and pour.

sentences.zh: 」言黃花不久也。

translations.literal: " It spoke of Yellow Flower not lasting long.
translations.idiomatic: " It meant that Yellow Flower would not last long.

sentences.zh: 後主自立穆後以後，昏飲無度，故云「清觴滿杯酌」。

translations.literal: After the later lord himself established Empress Mu, he drank in stupor without limit; hence "clear goblets fill the cup and pour."
translations.idiomatic: After the later lord himself established Empress Mu, he drank without measure in a stupor — hence "clear goblets fill to the brim and pour."

sentences.zh: 陸息駱提婆，詔改姓為穆；

translations.literal: Lu ended Luotipo and ordered the surname changed to Mu;
translations.idiomatic: Lu dismissed Luotipo and ordered his surname changed to Mu;

sentences.zh: 陸，太姬。

translations.literal: Lu, the Great Matriarch.
translations.idiomatic: Lu was styled the Great Matriarch.

sentences.zh: 皆以皇后故也。

translations.literal: All because of the empress.
translations.idiomatic: All of this was for the empress's sake.

sentences.zh: 後既以陸為母，提婆為家，更不采輕霄。

translations.literal: Afterward she took Lu as mother and Luotipo as family and no longer attended to Qingxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward she took Lu as her mother and Luotipo as her family, and no longer paid heed to Qingxiao.

sentences.zh: 輕霄後自療面，欲求見，為太姬陸媼使禁掌之，竟不得見。

translations.literal: Qingxiao later treated her own face to seek a meeting; Lady Lu the Great Matriarch had her imprisoned and guarded and in the end she could not be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxiao later tried to heal her face and beg for an audience; Lady Lu the Great Matriarch had her confined under guard, and she was never allowed to see her daughter.

sentences.zh: 馮淑妃名小憐，大穆後從婢也。

translations.literal: Consort Feng Shufei, named Xiaolian, was originally a attendant maid of the Great Empress Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Feng Shufei, named Xiaolian, had originally been a attendant maid of the Great Empress Mu.

sentences.zh: 穆後愛衰，以五月五日進之，號曰「續命」。

translations.literal: When the Great Empress Mu's love waned, on the fifth day of the fifth month she was presented — she was called "Extending Life."
translations.idiomatic: When Great Empress Mu's affection faded, on the fifth day of the fifth month Xiaolian was presented to the emperor under the name "Extending Life."

sentences.zh: 慧黠能彈琵琶，工歌舞。

translations.literal: Clever and able to play the pipa, skilled in song and dance.
translations.idiomatic: She was clever, played the pipa well, and excelled at song and dance.

sentences.zh: 後主惑之，坐則同席，出則並馬，願得生死一處。

translations.literal: The later lord was infatuated with her: seated they shared one mat; going out they shared one horse — wishing to live and die in one place.
translations.idiomatic: The later lord was infatuated: when seated they shared one mat; when they went out they rode the same horse — he wished never to be parted from her, in life or death.

sentences.zh: 命淑妃處隆基堂，淑妃惡曹昭儀所常居也，悉令反換其地。

translations.literal: He ordered the consort to dwell in Longji Hall; the consort hated what Consort Cao had often occupied — he had everything exchanged in place.
translations.idiomatic: He installed her in Longji Hall; she disliked the rooms Consort Cao had favored, and had all their furnishings swapped.

sentences.zh: 周師之取平陽，帝獵於三堆，晉州亟告急。

translations.literal: When Zhou troops took Pingyang the emperor was hunting at Sandui; Jinyang urgently reported danger.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou forces took Pingyang the emperor was hunting at Sandui; urgent dispatches arrived from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 帝將還，淑妃請更殺一圍，帝從其言。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to return; the consort requested one more round of the hunt and the emperor followed her word.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to return, but the consort asked for one more circuit of the hunt and he agreed.

sentences.zh: 識者以為後主名緯，殺圍言非吉征。

translations.literal: Those who understood thought that the later lord's name was Wei — "kill the encirclement" was not an auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: Observers noted that the later lord's personal name was Wei — the phrase for "finishing the hunt" also meant "kill the encirclement," an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 及帝至晉州，城已欲沒矣。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Jinyang the city was already on the verge of falling.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the emperor reached Jinyang the city was already on the brink of collapse.

sentences.zh: 作地道攻之，城陷十餘步，將士乘勢欲入。

translations.literal: They made a tunnel attack; the wall collapsed more than ten paces; soldiers riding the momentum wished to enter.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked by tunnel; the wall gave way for more than ten paces and the soldiers, seizing the moment, meant to rush in.

sentences.zh: 帝敕且止，召淑妃共觀之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered a halt for the moment and summoned the consort to watch together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered them to wait and summoned the consort to watch with him.

sentences.zh: 淑妃妝點，不獲時至。

translations.literal: The consort was applying makeup and could not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was still applying her makeup and could not come in time.

sentences.zh: 周人以木拒塞，城遂不下。

translations.literal: The Zhou men blocked it with timbers; the city thus was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou stuffed the breach with timbers; the city was not taken.

sentences.zh: 舊俗相傳，晉州城西石上有聖人跡，淑妃欲往觀之。

translations.literal: By old custom it was handed down that on the west of Jinyang city wall there was a sage's footprint on stone; the consort wished to go view it.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held that on the west side of Jinyang's city wall a sage's footprint was carved in stone; the consort wished to go see it.

sentences.zh: 帝恐弩矢及橋，故抽攻城木造遠橋，監作舍人以不速成受罰。

translations.literal: The emperor feared crossbow bolts would reach the bridge, so he pulled up the siege timbers to build a long bridge; the supervising builder was punished for not finishing quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing crossbow fire on the bridge, the emperor had siege timbers torn out to build a long bridge; the supervising craftsman was punished for slow work.

sentences.zh: 帝與淑妃度橋，橋壞，至夜乃還。

translations.literal: The emperor and consort crossed the bridge; the bridge broke; only at night did they return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and consort crossed the bridge; it collapsed; they did not return until night.

sentences.zh: 稱妃有功勳，將立為左皇后，即令使馳取禕翟等皇后服御。

translations.literal: He said the consort had merit and was about to establish her Left Empress; he immediately sent messengers galloping to fetch feather-embroidered robes and other empress regalia.
translations.idiomatic: He declared the consort had earned merit and was about to make her Left Empress; messengers were sent at once to fetch feather-embroidered robes and other empress regalia.

sentences.zh: 仍與之並騎觀戰，東偏少卻，淑妃怖曰：「軍敗矣！

translations.literal: Still he rode with her together to watch the battle; the eastern flank slightly gave way; the consort in fear said: "The army is defeated!
translations.idiomatic: He still rode with her to watch the battle; when the eastern flank wavered the consort cried in terror, "The army is beaten!

sentences.zh: 」帝遂以淑妃奔還。

translations.literal: " The emperor then fled back with the consort.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor at once fled back with her.

sentences.zh: 至洪洞戍，淑妃方以粉鏡自玩，後聲亂唱賊至，於是復走。

translations.literal: At Hongdong garrison the consort was just amusing herself with powder and mirror when behind them came chaotic cries that bandits had come; thereupon they fled again.
translations.idiomatic: At Hongdong garrison the consort was admiring herself in her mirror when confused shouts rose behind them that enemies had come; they fled again.

sentences.zh: 內參自晉陽以皇后衣至，帝為按轡，命淑妃著之，然後去。

translations.literal: Inner attendants from Jinyang brought the empress's robes; the emperor steadied the reins and ordered the consort to put them on, then left.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants from Jinyang brought the empress's robes; the emperor held the reins and made the consort dress in them before they rode on.

sentences.zh: 帝奔鄴，太后後至，帝不出迎；

translations.literal: The emperor fled to Ye; the empress dowager arrived later — the emperor did not go out to welcome her;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fled to Ye; the empress dowager arrived afterward — the emperor did not go out to welcome her;

sentences.zh: 淑妃將至，鑿城北門出十里迎之。

translations.literal: when the consort was about to arrive he broke open the north gate of the city and went out ten li to welcome her.
translations.idiomatic: but when the consort was about to arrive he had the north gate broken open and rode ten li out to welcome her.

sentences.zh: 復以淑妃奔青州。

translations.literal: Again he fled with the consort to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He fled again with the consort to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 後主至長安，請周武帝乞淑妃，帝曰：「朕視天下如脫屣，一老嫗豈與公惜也！

translations.literal: When the later lord reached Chang'an he begged Emperor Wu of Zhou for the consort; the emperor said: "I regard all under Heaven as cast-off shoes — would I begrudge an old woman to you!
translations.idiomatic: When the later lord reached Chang'an he begged Emperor Wu of Zhou for the consort; the emperor said, "I regard all under Heaven as shoes I have cast off — would I begrudge you one old woman!

sentences.zh: 」仍以賜之。

translations.literal: " He still bestowed her on him.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave her to him nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 及帝遇害，以淑妃賜代王達，甚嬖之。

translations.literal: When the emperor met disaster the consort was bestowed on Prince of Dai Da; he was greatly infatuated with her.
translations.idiomatic: When the later lord was killed the consort was given to Prince of Dai, Da, who doted on her greatly.

sentences.zh: 淑妃彈琵琶，因弦斷，作詩曰：「雖蒙今日寵，猶憶昔時憐。

translations.literal: The consort played the pipa; because a string broke she composed a poem: "Though I enjoy today's favor, I still recall former tenderness.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was playing the pipa when a string snapped; she composed a poem: "Though I enjoy today's favor, I still recall former tenderness.

sentences.zh: 欲知心斷絕，應看膠上弦。

translations.literal: If you wish to know the heart's severance, look at the glue on the broken string.
translations.idiomatic: If you would know how the heart is severed, look at the glue on the broken string.

sentences.zh: 」達妃為淑妃所譖，幾致於死。

translations.literal: " Da's consort was slandered by the consort and nearly came to death.
translations.idiomatic: " Prince Da's own consort was slandered by her and nearly died for it.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝將賜達妃兄李詢，令著布裙配舂。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was about to bestow her on Da's consort's brother Li Xun, he ordered her to wear cloth skirts and be paired to pound grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was about to give her to Prince Da's consort's brother Li Xun, he ordered her to wear cloth skirts and be paired with him to pound grain at the mortar.

sentences.zh: 詢母逼令自殺。

translations.literal: Xun's mother forced her to kill herself.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's mother drove her to suicide.

sentences.zh: 後主以李祖欽女為左昭儀，進為左娥英。

translations.literal: The later lord took Li Zuqin's daughter as Left Zhaoyi and advanced her to Left Eying.
translations.idiomatic: The later lord took Li Zuqin's daughter as Left Zhaoyi and promoted her to Left Eying.

sentences.zh: 裴氏為右娥英。

translations.literal: Lady Pei was Right Eying.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pei was made Right Eying.

sentences.zh: 娥英者，兼取舜妃娥皇、女英名，陽休之所制。

translations.literal: Eying — taking together the names of Shun's consorts Ehuang and Nuying — was Yang Xiuzhi's coinage.
