translations.idiomatic: The title Eying, combining the names of Shun's consorts Ehuang and Nuying, was Yang Xiuzhi's invention.

sentences.zh: 樂人曹僧奴進二女，大者忤旨，剝面皮；

translations.literal: Musician Cao Sengnu presented two daughters; the elder offended the will and had her face skinned;
translations.idiomatic: The musician Cao Sengnu presented two daughters; the elder offended the emperor and had the skin of her face stripped away;

sentences.zh: 少者彈琵琶，為昭儀。

translations.literal: the younger played the pipa and became zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: the younger played the pipa and was made zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 以僧奴為日南王。

translations.literal: Sengnu was made Prince of Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: Sengnu was enfeoffed as Prince of Rinan.

sentences.zh: 僧奴死後，又貴其兄弟妙達等二人，同日皆為郡王。

translations.literal: After Sengnu's death he again honored his brothers Miaoda and two others; on the same day all were made princes of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: After Sengnu died the emperor again favored his brothers Miaoda and two others; on a single day all three were made princes of commanderies.

sentences.zh: 為昭儀別起隆基堂，極為綺麗。

translations.literal: For the zhaoyi he separately raised Longji Hall, extremely ornate and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: For the zhaoyi he built a separate Longji Hall, lavish beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 陸媼誣以左道，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Lady Lu slandered her with left-hand ways and she was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Lu accused her of sorcery and she was executed.

sentences.zh: 又有董昭儀、毛夫人、彭夫人、王夫人、小王夫人、二李夫人，皆嬖寵之。

translations.literal: There were also Consort Dong, Lady Mao, Lady Peng, Lady Wang, the Lesser Lady Wang, and two Ladies Li — all were greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Consort Dong, Lady Mao, Lady Peng, Lady Wang, the Lesser Lady Wang, and two Ladies Li — all were greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 毛能彈箏，本和士開薦入。

translations.literal: Mao could play the zither; she had originally been recommended by He Shikai.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Mao could play the zither; He Shikai had originally recommended her.

sentences.zh: 帝所幸彭夫人，亦音妓進；

translations.literal: The emperor favored Lady Peng, who had also entered as a musical performer;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored Lady Peng, who had entered the palace as a musical performer;

sentences.zh: 死于晉陽，造佛寺，與總持相埒。

translations.literal: she died at Jinyang; a Buddhist temple was built, rivaling the Zongchi.
translations.idiomatic: she died at Jinyang, and a Buddhist temple was built to rival the Zongchi.

sentences.zh: 一李是隸戶女，以五弦進。

translations.literal: One Li was the daughter of a bondservant household and entered with the five-string.
translations.idiomatic: One Lady Li was the daughter of a bondservant household and was presented for her skill on the five-string.

sentences.zh: 一李即孝貞之女也。

translations.literal: One Li was Xiaozheng's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The other Lady Li was Xiaozheng's daughter.

sentences.zh: 小王生一，男，諸閹人在傍，皆蒙賜給。

translations.literal: The Lesser Wang bore one son; the eunuchs beside her all received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Lady Wang bore a son; the eunuchs in attendance all received rewards.

sentences.zh: 毛兄思安，超登武衛。

translations.literal: Mao's elder brother Sian was abruptly promoted to Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Mao's elder brother Sian was abruptly promoted to the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 董父賢義，為作軍主，由昭儀亦超登開府。

translations.literal: Dong's father Xianyi was made army commander; through the zhaoyi he also abruptly rose to opening the government.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Dong's father Xianyi was made an army commander; through his daughter he too was suddenly elevated to opening the government.

sentences.zh: 自餘姻屬，多至大官。

translations.literal: The rest of the affinal kin mostly reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: Other relatives by marriage likewise rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 北朝周

translations.literal: Northern Dynasties — Zhou
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Dynasties: Zhou

sentences.zh: 周文皇后元氏，魏孝武之妹也。

translations.literal: Empress Yuan of Zhou Wen was a younger sister of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuan of Zhou Wen was a younger sister of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei.

sentences.zh: 初封平原公主，適開府張歡。

translations.literal: At first enfeoffed Princess of Pingyuan, she was married to Zhang Huan, opening the government.
translations.idiomatic: First enfeoffed as Princess of Pingyuan, she was married to Zhang Huan, a commander of the opening-the-government rank.

sentences.zh: 歡性貪殘，遇後無禮。

translations.literal: Huan's nature was greedy and cruel; toward the empress he was without propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was greedy and cruel and treated the empress without proper respect.

sentences.zh: 帝殺歡，改封後為馮翊公主，以配周文帝。

translations.literal: The emperor killed Huan and changed the empress's enfeoffment to Princess of Fengyi, matching her to Zhou Wendi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor executed Huan, changed her title to Princess of Fengyi, and gave her in marriage to Zhou Wendi.

sentences.zh: 生孝閔帝。

translations.literal: She bore Emperor Xiaomin.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Emperor Xiaomin.

sentences.zh: 魏大統十七年，薨。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Great Unity of Wei she died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Great Unity of Wei she died.

sentences.zh: 恭帝三年十二月，合葬成陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of the Gongdi era she was buried together at Chengling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year of the Gongdi era she was buried with him at Chengling.

sentences.zh: 孝閔踐阼，追尊為王后。

translations.literal: When Xiaomin took the throne he posthumously honored her as queen.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaomin took the throne he posthumously honored her as queen.

sentences.zh: 武成初，又追尊為皇后。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng she was again posthumously honored as empress.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wucheng she was again posthumously honored as empress.

sentences.zh: 文宣皇后叱奴氏，代人也。

translations.literal: Empress Chinu of Wenzuan was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chinu of Wenzuan was from Dai.

sentences.zh: 周文帝為丞相，納為姬，生武帝。

translations.literal: When Zhou Wendi was chief minister he took her as a concubine; she bore Wudi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Wendi was chief minister he took her as a concubine; she bore Wudi.

sentences.zh: 天和二年六月，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Tianhe she was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Tianhe she was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 建德三年三月，崩。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Jiande she died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Jiande she died.

sentences.zh: 五月，葬永固陵。

translations.literal: In the fifth month she was buried at Yonggu Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month she was buried at Yonggu Tomb.

sentences.zh: 明敬皇后獨孤氏，太保、衛公信之長女也。

translations.literal: Empress Dugu of Mingjing was the eldest daughter of Grand Guardian and Duke of Wei Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dugu of Mingjing was the eldest daughter of the Grand Guardian and Duke of Wei, Xin.

sentences.zh: 帝之在籓，納為夫人。

translations.literal: When the emperor was in his princedom he took her as lady.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was still a prince he took her as his lady.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，立為王后。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year she was established queen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year she was made queen.

sentences.zh: 四月，崩，葬昭陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month she died and was buried at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month she died and was buried at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 武成初，追崇為皇后。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng she was posthumously honored as empress.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wucheng she was posthumously honored as empress.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，與後合葬焉。

translations.literal: When Mingdi died she was buried together with the empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingdi died she was buried together with him.

sentences.zh: 武成皇后阿史那氏，突厥木杆可汗俟斤之女也。

translations.literal: Empress Ashina of Wucheng was the daughter of the Türk qaghan Muqan, son of Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ashina of Wucheng was the daughter of the Türk qaghan Muqan.

sentences.zh: 突厥滅蠕蠕後，盡有塞表之地，志陵中夏。

translations.literal: After the Türk destroyed the Rouran they wholly possessed the lands beyond the frontier; their ambition reached into the central plains.
translations.idiomatic: After the Türk destroyed the Rouran they held all the lands beyond the frontier and turned their ambition toward the central plains.

sentences.zh: 周文方與齊人爭衡。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen was then contending with the Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen was then locked in rivalry with Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 結以為援。

translations.literal: He allied with them as aid.
translations.idiomatic: He allied with the Türk for support.

sentences.zh: 俟斤初欲以女配帝，既而悔之。

translations.literal: Qaghan at first wished to give his daughter to the emperor, then afterward regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Qaghan at first intended to give his daughter to the Zhou emperor, then changed his mind.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，前後累遣使焉。

translations.literal: When Wudi took the throne envoys were repeatedly sent.
translations.idiomatic: When Wudi took the throne envoys were sent again and again.

sentences.zh: 保定五年二月，詔陳公純。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year of Baoding an edict ordered Duke of Chen Chun,
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year of Baoding an edict ordered the Duke of Chen, Chun,

sentences.zh: 許公于文貴、神武公竇毅、南安公楊薦等，備皇后文物及行殿，並六宮以下一百二十人，至俟斤牙所迎後。

translations.literal: Duke of Xu Yu Wengui, Duke of Shenwu Dou Yi, Duke of Nan'an Yang Jian, and others, to prepare the empress's ritual objects and traveling hall, together with the six palaces below — one hundred twenty persons — and go to Qaghan's camp to welcome the empress.
translations.idiomatic: the Duke of Xu Yu Wengui, the Duke of Shenwu Dou Yi, the Duke of Nan'an Yang Jian, and others to prepare the empress's ritual regalia and traveling pavilion, together with the full six-palace retinue of one hundred twenty persons, and proceed to Qaghan's camp to welcome the empress.

sentences.zh: 俟斤又許齊婚，將有異志，純等累請，不得反命。

translations.literal: Qaghan again promised marriage to Qi and was about to harbor a different intent; Chun and the rest repeatedly requested but could not return with their mission accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Qaghan also promised his daughter to Qi and was about to shift allegiance; Chun and the others pleaded repeatedly but could not obtain leave to return.

sentences.zh: 會雷風大起，飄壞其穹廬，俟斤大懼，以為天譴，乃禮送後，純等奉之以歸。

translations.literal: Thunder and wind suddenly arose and blew down their yurt; Qaghan was greatly afraid, taking it as heaven's punishment, and then with ritual sent off the empress; Chun and the rest escorted her back.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly thunder and wind arose and blew down their yurt; Qaghan was terrified, taking it as heaven's punishment, and then ceremonially sent the empress off; Chun and the others escorted her home.

sentences.zh: 天和三年三月至，武帝接以親迎之禮。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Tianhe she arrived; Wudi received her with the rites of greeting the bride in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Tianhe she arrived; Wudi received her with the rites of personally greeting the bride.

sentences.zh: 後有姿貌，善容止，帝深敬禮焉。

translations.literal: The empress had beauty and grace in bearing; the emperor deeply honored and treated her with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was beautiful and graceful in deportment; the emperor treated her with deep respect and ceremony.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，尊後為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Xuandi took the throne the empress was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuandi took the throne she was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 大象元年二月，改為天元皇太后。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Daxiang she was changed to Heavenly Yuan Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Daxiang she was styled Heavenly Yuan Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，又尊曰天元上皇太后。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year she was again honored as Heavenly Yuan Supreme Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year she was further honored as Heavenly Yuan Supreme Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 宣帝崩，靜帝尊為太皇太后。

translations.literal: When Xuandi died Jingdi honored her as grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuandi died, Jingdi honored her as grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇二年，殂，年三十二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaihuang of Sui she died, age thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaihuang under the Sui she died, aged thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 隋文詔有司備禮，祔葬後於孝陵。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui ordered the authorities to prepare rites and bury her attached at Xiaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen ordered the authorities to prepare rites and bury her beside Xiaoling.

sentences.zh: 宣皇后楊氏名麗華，隋文帝之長女也。

translations.literal: Empress Yang of Xuandi, named Lihua, was the eldest daughter of Emperor Wen of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang of Xuandi, named Lihua, was the eldest daughter of Emperor Wen of Sui.

sentences.zh: 帝在東宮，武帝為帝納後為皇太子妃。

translations.literal: When the emperor was in the eastern palace Wudi had the emperor take her as crown prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was crown prince, Wudi had him take her as crown princess.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年閏六月，並為皇后。

translations.literal: In the intercalary sixth month of the first year of Xuanzheng she was together established empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary sixth month of the first year of Xuanzheng she was made empress together with him.

sentences.zh: 帝后自稱天元皇帝，號後為天元皇后。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress each styled themselves Heavenly Yuan Emperor and Heavenly Yuan Empress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress each styled themselves Heavenly Yuan Emperor and Heavenly Yuan Empress.

sentences.zh: 尋又立天皇后及左右皇后，與為四皇后。

translations.literal: Soon he also established Heavenly Empress and Left and Right empresses — four empresses in all.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also established a Heavenly Empress and Left and Right empresses — four empresses in all.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，詔取象四星，於是後及三皇后並加大焉。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year an edict took the four stars as model; thereupon the empress and the three empresses all received greater titles.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year an edict took the four stars as its model; the empress and the three other empresses all received elevated titles.

sentences.zh: 冊授後為天元大皇后，又立天中大皇后，與後為五皇后焉。

translations.literal: The empress was invested as Heavenly Yuan Great Empress; he also established Heavenly Central Great Empress — five empresses in all.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was invested as Heavenly Yuan Great Empress; a Heavenly Central Great Empress was also established — five empresses in all.

sentences.zh: 後性柔婉，不妒忌，四皇后及嬪御等咸愛而仰之。

translations.literal: The empress's nature was gentle and yielding, without jealousy; the four empresses and consorts all loved and looked up to her.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was gentle and unjealous; the four empresses and all the consorts loved and revered her.

sentences.zh: 帝後昏暴滋甚，喜怒乖度。

translations.literal: The emperor afterward grew ever more violent and depraved; joy and anger lost measure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew ever more violent and depraved; his moods knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 嘗譴後，欲加之罪，後進止詳閑，辭色不撓。

translations.literal: Once he reproached the empress and wished to punish her; the empress in advancing and withdrawing was detailed and composed, in words and color unbending.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reproached the empress and meant to punish her; she remained composed in bearing and unyielding in tone.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，遂賜後死，逼令自引決。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and then ordered the empress to die, forcing her to take her own life.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered her to die, forcing her to kill herself.

sentences.zh: 後母獨孤氏聞之，詣閣陳謝，叩頭流血，然後得免。

translations.literal: The empress's mother Lady Dugu heard of it, went to the gate to plead guilt, knocked her head until it bled, and only then was she spared.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Lady Dugu heard of it, went to the palace gate to plead, knocked her head until it bled, and only then was the empress spared.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，靜帝尊後為皇太后，居弘聖宮。

translations.literal: When the emperor died Jingdi honored the empress as empress dowager; she dwelt in Hongsheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died Jingdi honored her as empress dowager; she lived in Hongsheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 初，宣帝不豫，詔隋文帝入禁中侍疾。

translations.literal: Earlier when Xuandi was ill he ordered Emperor Wen of Sui to enter the forbidden quarters to attend his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xuandi fell ill, he had summoned Emperor Wen of Sui into the inner palace to attend him.

sentences.zh: 及大漸，劉昉、鄭譯等因矯詔以隋文帝受遺輔政。

translations.literal: At the approach of death Liu Fang and Zheng Yi and others through a forged edict had Emperor Wen of Sui receive the testamentary regency.
translations.idiomatic: As death approached, Liu Fang and Zheng Yi forged an edict placing Emperor Wen of Sui in charge as regent.

sentences.zh: 後初雖不預謀，然以嗣主幼沖，恐權在他族，不利於己，聞昉、譯已行此詔，心甚悅。

translations.literal: The empress at first had not taken part in the plot, yet because the heir was young she feared power would rest in another clan, not benefiting herself; when she heard Fang and Yi had already carried out this edict her heart was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had not plotted at first, but because the heir was young she feared power would pass to another house; when she learned Fang and Yi had already issued the edict she was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 後知隋文有異圖，意頗不平。

translations.literal: Later she knew Emperor Wen harbored a different design and her heart was quite uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when she saw that Emperor Wen harbored designs of his own, she grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 及行禪代，憤惋愈甚。

translations.literal: When the abdication was carried out her anger and grief grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne was seized her anger and grief only deepened.

sentences.zh: 隋文內甚愧之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen inwardly was deeply ashamed toward her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen felt deep shame toward her in his heart.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，封後為樂平公主。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang she was enfeoffed Princess of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang she was enfeoffed as Princess of Leping.

sentences.zh: 後又議奪其志，後誓不許，乃止。

translations.literal: Later they again discussed seizing her will; the empress swore she would not permit it and they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Later there was talk of forcing her to remarry; she swore she would never consent, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 大業五年，從煬帝幸張掖，殂於河西。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye she followed Emperor Yang to Zhangye and died in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daye she accompanied Emperor Yang to Zhangye and died in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 詔還京，所司備禮，祔葬後於定陵。

translations.literal: An edict ordered return to the capital; the authorities prepared rites and buried her attached at Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered her remains returned to the capital; the authorities prepared rites and buried her beside Dingling.

sentences.zh: 宣帝后硃氏，名滿月，吳人也。

translations.literal: Xuandi's empress Zhu, named Manyue, was a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xuandi's empress Zhu, named Manyue, was from Wu.

sentences.zh: 其家坐事，沒入東宮。

translations.literal: Her family because of a case was confiscated and entered the eastern palace.
translations.idiomatic: Her family, implicated in a crime, was confiscated and she was sent into the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 宣帝之為太子，後被選掌衣服，帝召幸之，遂生靜帝。

translations.literal: When Xuandi was crown prince the empress was chosen to manage clothing; the emperor summoned and favored her; she then bore Jingdi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuandi was crown prince she was chosen to manage his wardrobe; he summoned and favored her, and she bore Jingdi.

sentences.zh: 大象元年四月，立為天元帝后。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Daxiang she was established Heavenly Yuan Imperial Empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Daxiang she was made Heavenly Yuan Imperial Empress.

sentences.zh: 七月，改為天皇后。

translations.literal: In the seventh month she was changed to Heavenly Empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month she was restyled Heavenly Empress.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，又改為天大皇后。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year she was again changed to Heavenly Great Empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year she was again restyled Heavenly Great Empress.

sentences.zh: 後本非良家子，又年長於帝十餘歲，疏賤無寵。

translations.literal: The empress was originally not of a good family; she was also more than ten years older than the emperor — distant, lowly, without favor.
translations.idiomatic: She was not from a respectable family and was more than ten years older than the emperor — kept at a distance, low in rank, without favor.

sentences.zh: 以靜帝故，特尊崇之，班亞楊皇后焉。

translations.literal: Because of Jingdi she was especially honored; her rank was second only to Empress Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Jingdi she was specially honored; her rank stood just below Empress Yang.

sentences.zh: 宣帝崩，靜帝尊後為帝太后。

translations.literal: When Xuandi died Jingdi honored the empress as imperial empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuandi died Jingdi honored her as imperial empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇元年二月，出俗為尼，改名法靜。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Kaihuang of Sui she left the laity and became a nun, changing her name to Fajing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Kaihuang she left secular life and became a nun, taking the name Fajing.

sentences.zh: 六年，殂，以尼禮葬於京城西。

translations.literal: In the sixth year she died and was buried west of the capital with nun's rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year she died and was buried west of the capital with the rites of a nun.

sentences.zh: 後父晟，少以元氏宗室，拜開府。

translations.literal: The empress's father Sheng, in youth because of the Yuan clan's imperial house, was appointed opening the government.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Sheng, as a young man of the Yuan imperial clan, was appointed commander of the opening-the-government rank.

sentences.zh: 大象元年七月，以後父進位上柱國，封翼國公。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Daxiang, because he was the empress's father he was advanced to supreme pillar of state and enfeoffed Duke of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Daxiang, as the empress's father, he was promoted to supreme pillar of state and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.

sentences.zh: 宣帝皇后尉遲氏名繁熾，蜀公迥之孫女也。

translations.literal: Xuandi's empress Yuchi, named Fanchi, was the granddaughter of Duke of Shu Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Xuandi's empress Yuchi, named Fanchi, was the granddaughter of the Duke of Shu, Jiong.

sentences.zh: 有美色。

translations.literal: She had beautiful looks.
translations.idiomatic: She was renowned for her beauty.

sentences.zh: 初適杞公亮子西陽公溫，以宗婦例入朝，帝逼幸之。

translations.literal: At first she was married to Xi Yanggong Wen, son of Duke of Qi Liang; by the precedent for clan wives she entered court; the emperor forced and favored her.
translations.idiomatic: She had first been married to Wen, son of Duke of Qi Liang, bearing the title Lady of Xi Yang; as a clan wife she entered court on the usual rounds, where the emperor forced himself on her.

sentences.zh: 及亮謀逆，帝誅溫，追後入宮，拜長貴妃。

translations.literal: When Liang plotted rebellion the emperor executed Wen and pursued the empress into the palace, appointing her Senior Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang plotted rebellion the emperor executed Wen, brought her into the palace, and made her Senior Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 大象二年三月，立為天左大皇后。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Daxiang she was established Heavenly Left Great Empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Daxiang she was made Heavenly Left Great Empress.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，後出俗為尼，改名華道。

translations.literal: When the emperor died the empress left the laity and became a nun, changing her name to Huadao.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died she left secular life and became a nun, taking the name Huadao.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇十五年，殂。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kaihuang of Sui she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the fifteenth year of Kaihuang.

sentences.zh: 隋文獻皇后獨孤氏，諱伽羅，河南洛陽人，周大司馬、衛公信之女也。

translations.literal: Empress Dugu the Literary of Sui, tabooed Jialuo, was a man of Luoyang in Henan, daughter of Grand Marshal and Duke of Wei Xin of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dugu the Literary of Sui, taboo name Jialuo, was from Luoyang in Henan, daughter of Zhou's Grand Marshal and Duke of Wei, Xin.

sentences.zh: 信見文帝有奇表，故以後妻焉。

translations.literal: Xin saw Wendi had an extraordinary countenance and therefore gave him the empress as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Xin saw that Wendi bore an extraordinary countenance and gave him Jialuo as his wife.

sentences.zh: 時年十四。

translations.literal: She was then fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: She was fourteen at the time.

sentences.zh: 帝與後相得，誓無異生之子。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress were well matched; they swore no children by another.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor and empress were devoted to each other and swore they would have no children by anyone else.

sentences.zh: 後姊為周明帝后，長女為周宣帝后；

translations.literal: The empress's elder sister was empress to Zhou Mingdi; the eldest daughter was empress to Zhou Xuandi;
translations.idiomatic: Her elder sister became empress to Zhou Mingdi; her eldest daughter became empress to Zhou Xuandi;

sentences.zh: 貴戚之盛，莫與為比，而後每謙卑自守。

translations.literal: the glory of noble kin — none could compare — yet the empress each time kept humble self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: no family of imperial kin could match their glory — yet the empress always remained humble and restrained.

sentences.zh: 及周宣帝崩，隋文居禁中，總百揆。

translations.literal: When Zhou Xuandi died Wendi dwelt in the forbidden quarters and held all government.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Xuandi died Wendi held the inner palace and directed all government.

sentences.zh: 後使李圓通謂文帝曰：「騎獸之勢，必不得下，勉之！

translations.literal: The empress sent Li Yuantong to tell Wendi: "One who rides a beast cannot dismount — exert yourself!
translations.idiomatic: The empress sent Li Yuantong to tell him, "Once you mount the beast you cannot dismount — press on!

sentences.zh: 」及帝受禪，立為皇后。

translations.literal: " When the emperor received the abdication she was established empress.
translations.idiomatic: " When he took the throne she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 突厥嘗與中國交市，有明珠一篋，價直八百萬；

translations.literal: The Türk once traded with the central states; there was a basket of bright pearls worth eight million.
translations.idiomatic: The Türk once traded with the central states; a basket of luminous pearls was offered at eight million.

sentences.zh: 幽州總管陰壽白後市之。

translations.literal: Regional commander of Youzhou Yin Shou reported to the empress to buy them.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commander of Youzhou, Yin Shou, asked the empress to purchase them.

sentences.zh: 後曰：「當今戎狄屢寇，將士罷勞，未若以八百萬分賞有功者。

translations.literal: The empress said: "Nowadays the barbarians repeatedly raid; soldiers and officers are weary — better to divide the eight million as reward for those with merit.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "The frontier tribes raid again and again and the troops are exhausted — better to divide the eight million among those who have earned merit.

sentences.zh: 」百寮聞而畢賀。

translations.literal: " All officials hearing it completely congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: " All the officials, hearing this, offered their congratulations.

sentences.zh: 文帝甚寵憚之。

translations.literal: Wendi greatly favored and also feared her.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi both doted on her and stood in awe of her.

sentences.zh: 帝每臨朝，後輒與上方輦而進，至閣乃止。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor attended court the empress always rode up with him in the imperial carriage to the gate and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor held court the empress rode with him in the imperial carriage as far as the gate, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 使宮官伺帝，政有所失，隨則匡諫，多所弘益。

translations.literal: She had palace officers watch the emperor; when governance went astray she at once corrected and remonstrated — much was broadly benefited.
translations.idiomatic: She had palace officers watch him; when his governance went astray she corrected and remonstrated at once — to great benefit.

sentences.zh: 候帝退朝而同反宴寢，相顧欣然。

translations.literal: She waited until the emperor left court and together returned to feast and sleep, looking at each other with pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: She waited until he left court and they returned together to feast and sleep, regarding each other with quiet joy.

sentences.zh: 後早失二親，常懷感慕，見公卿有父母者，每為致禮焉。

translations.literal: The empress early lost both parents and always cherished longing; seeing ministers and grandees who had parents she often extended courtesy to them.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost both parents early she always cherished their memory; when she met ministers who still had parents she often showed them special courtesy.

sentences.zh: 有司奏曰：「《周禮》，百官之妻，命于王后。

translations.literal: The authorities memorialized: "In the Zhou Rites, the wives of the hundred officials receive appointment from the queen.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities memorialized, "In the Zhou Rites, the wives of the hundred officials receive appointment from the queen.

sentences.zh: 憲章在昔，請依古制。

translations.literal: The statutes and models are in the past — please follow the ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: The statutes of old are on record — we ask that the ancient system be followed.

sentences.zh: 」後曰：「以婦人與政，或從此漸，不可開其源也。

translations.literal: " The empress said: "To let women join in government may begin from this — the source cannot be opened.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress said, "To let women share in government may begin with this step — that door must not be opened.

sentences.zh: 」不許。

translations.literal: " She did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " She refused.

sentences.zh: 後每謂諸公主曰：「周家公主類無婦德，失禮于舅姑，離薄人骨肉，此不順事，爾等當誡之。

translations.literal: The empress often told the princesses: "The princesses of the Zhou house mostly lacked wifely virtue, were without ritual toward parents-in-law, and estranged kin from flesh — this is not the compliant way; you must warn against it.
translations.idiomatic: She often told the princesses, "The Zhou princesses mostly lacked wifely virtue, failed in ritual toward their husbands' parents, and drove wedges between kin — you must guard against such conduct.

sentences.zh: 」後姑子都督崔長仁犯法當斬，文帝以後故免之。

translations.literal: The empress's cousin by marriage Colonel Cui Changren violated the law and should have been beheaded; Wendi because of the empress pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Her cousin by marriage, Colonel Cui Changren, committed a capital crime; Wendi would have pardoned him for the empress's sake.

sentences.zh: 後曰：「國家之事，焉可顧私！

translations.literal: The empress said: "State affairs — how can one look to private ties!
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "These are affairs of state — how can one favor private ties!

sentences.zh: 」長仁竟坐死。

translations.literal: " Changren in the end died for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: " Changren was executed in the end.

sentences.zh: 異母弟陀以貓鬼巫蠱咒詛於後，坐當死。

translations.literal: Her younger half-brother Tuo by cat-demon witchcraft cursed the empress and for it should have died.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger half-brother Tuo used cat-demon sorcery to curse her and was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 後三日不食，為之請命曰：「陀若蠹政害民者，不敢言。

translations.literal: The empress for three days did not eat and pleaded for his life saying: "If Tuo by corrupting government and harming the people — I dare not speak.
translations.idiomatic: For three days she ate nothing and pleaded for his life: "If Tuo harmed the people or corrupted government I would not speak.

sentences.zh: 今坐為妾身，請其命。

translations.literal: Now the crime is for my person — I beg his life.
translations.idiomatic: But his crime was against me alone — I beg for his life.

sentences.zh: 」陀於是減死一等。

translations.literal: " Tuo was thereby reduced one degree from death.
translations.idiomatic: " Tuo's sentence was reduced one degree from death.

sentences.zh: 後雅性儉約。

translations.literal: The empress by nature was elegant and frugal.
translations.idiomatic: By nature she was elegant and frugal.

sentences.zh: 帝常合止利藥，須胡粉一兩，宮內不用，求之竟不得。

translations.literal: The emperor often compounded restorative medicine and needed one tael of barbarian powder; within the palace none was used — seeking it, in the end it could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often prepared restorative medicines needing one tael of barbarian powder; the inner palace kept none in stock and none could be found.

sentences.zh: 又欲賜柱國劉嵩妻織成衣領，宮內亦無。

translations.literal: He also wished to bestow on Pillar of State Liu Song's wife a woven collar — within the palace there was also none.
translations.idiomatic: He also wished to give Pillar of State Liu Song's wife a woven collar — the inner palace had none of those either.

sentences.zh: 上以後不好華麗，時齊七寶車及鏡臺絕巧麗，使毀車而以鏡臺賜後。

translations.literal: The emperor because the empress did not love splendor — at the time Qi's seven-jewel carriage and mirror stand were supremely clever and beautiful — had the carriage destroyed and the mirror stand bestowed on the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Because she disliked luxury, when a supremely fine seven-jewel carriage and mirror stand from Qi arrived, the emperor had the carriage destroyed and gave her only the mirror stand.

sentences.zh: 後雅好讀書，識達今古，凡言事皆與上意合，宮中稱為二聖。

translations.literal: The empress elegantly loved reading; penetrating in present and past — whatever she spoke all matched the emperor's intent; within the palace they were called the Two Sages.
translations.idiomatic: She loved books and understood present and past; whatever she advised matched the emperor's mind — within the palace they were called the Two Sages.

sentences.zh: 嘗夢周阿史那後，言受罪辛苦，求營功德。

translations.literal: Once she dreamed of Zhou's Empress Ashina, who said she suffered bitter punishment and begged merit to be performed.
translations.idiomatic: Once she dreamed of Zhou's Empress Ashina, who said she was suffering bitter punishment and begged that merit be performed for her.

sentences.zh: 明日言之，上為立寺追福焉。

translations.literal: The next day she spoke of it; the emperor for her established a temple to pursue blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The next day she told the emperor, who had a temple built to transfer merit on her behalf.

sentences.zh: 後兄女，夫死於并州，後嫂以女有娠，請不赴葬。

translations.literal: The empress's elder brother's daughter — her husband died at Bingzhou; the empress's sister-in-law because the girl was pregnant asked that she not go to the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Her brother's daughter, whose husband had died at Bingzhou, was pregnant; the girl's mother-in-law asked that she not attend the funeral.

sentences.zh: 後曰：「婦人事夫，何容不往！

translations.literal: The empress said: "A woman's affair is serving the husband — how can she not go!
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "A woman's duty is to serve her husband — how can she stay away!

sentences.zh: 其姑在，宜自諮之。

translations.literal: If her mother-in-law is present, she should consult her herself.
translations.idiomatic: If her mother-in-law is there, let her ask her directly.

sentences.zh: 」姑不許，女遂行。

translations.literal: " The mother-in-law did not permit it; the girl then went.
translations.idiomatic: " The mother-in-law refused; the girl went anyway.

sentences.zh: 後頗仁愛，每聞大理決囚，未嘗不流涕。

translations.literal: The empress was quite benevolent and loving; whenever she heard the Court of Review decide prisoners she never failed to shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: She was deeply benevolent; whenever she heard the Court of Review pass sentence she wept.

sentences.zh: 然性尤妒忌，後宮莫敢進禦。

translations.literal: Yet her nature was especially jealous; within the rear palace none dared approach the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet she was fiercely jealous; no woman in the rear palace dared approach the emperor.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥女孫有美色，先在宮中，帝于仁壽宮見而悅之，因得幸。

translations.literal: The granddaughter of Yuchi Jiong had beautiful looks; she was first in the palace; the emperor at Renshou Palace saw and was pleased with her and thereby won favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong's granddaughter, a great beauty, was already in the palace; the emperor saw her at Renshou Palace, took a liking to her, and favored her.

sentences.zh: 後伺帝聽朝，陰殺之。

translations.literal: The empress waited until the emperor attended court and secretly killed her.
translations.idiomatic: The empress waited until he went to court and had her killed in secret.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，單騎從苑中出，不由徑路，入山谷間三十餘里。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, rode alone from the park out, not by the path, and entered a mountain valley more than thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, rode alone out of the park by no proper path, and wandered more than thirty li into the hills.

sentences.zh: 高熲、楊素等追及，扣馬諫。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong, Yang Su, and others pursued and caught up, seized the horse's bridle and remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong, Yang Su, and others caught up, seized his bridle, and remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 帝太息曰：「吾貴為天子，不得自由！

translations.literal: The emperor sighed deeply and said: "I am honored as Son of Heaven yet cannot be free!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said, "I am honored as Son of Heaven yet I am not free!

sentences.zh: 」高熲曰：「陛下豈以一婦人而輕天下？

translations.literal: " Gao Jiong said: "Your Majesty — how can you lightly regard all under Heaven for one woman?
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Jiong said, "Your Majesty — how can you slight the empire for one woman?

sentences.zh: 」帝意少解，駐馬良久，夜方還宮。

translations.literal: " The emperor's intent slightly eased; he halted his horse a long while; only at night did he return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's anger eased somewhat; he halted a long while and returned to the palace only at night.

sentences.zh: 後候上於閣內，及帝至，流涕拜謝。

translations.literal: The empress waited for the emperor inside the gate; when the emperor arrived she wept and bowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: The empress waited inside the gate; when he arrived she wept and bowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 熲、素等和解之，上置酒極歡。

translations.literal: Jiong, Su, and others reconciled them; the emperor set out wine and was extremely merry.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong, Su, and the others mediated; the emperor set out wine and they were merry again.

sentences.zh: 後自此意頗折。

translations.literal: From this the empress's intent was quite broken.
translations.idiomatic: From that time her jealousy was somewhat curbed.

sentences.zh: 仁壽二年八月甲子，日暈四重。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Renshou, on the day jiazi, the sun had halos in four rings.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Renshou, on the day jiazi, the sun showed halos in four rings.

sentences.zh: 己巳。

translations.literal: On the day jisi.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jisi.

sentences.zh: 太白犯軒轅。

translations.literal: Great White invaded the Bushel.
translations.idiomatic: The planet Venus crossed the Bushel constellation.

sentences.zh: 其夜，後崩于永安宮，時年五十九，葬於太陵。

translations.literal: That night the empress died in Yong'an Palace, age fifty-nine; she was buried at Tailing.
translations.idiomatic: That night the empress died in Yong'an Palace, aged fifty-nine, and was buried at Tailing.

sentences.zh: 其後宣華夫人陳氏、容華夫人蔡氏俱有寵，帝頗惑之，由是發疾。

translations.literal: Afterward Lady Xuanhua Chen and Lady Ronghua Cai both had favor; the emperor was quite infatuated — because of this illness arose.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Lady Xuanhua Chen and Lady Ronghua Cai both won favor; the emperor was deeply infatuated — illness followed.

sentences.zh: 及危篤，謂侍者曰「使皇后在，吾不及此」云。

translations.literal: At the approach of death he told attendants: "Had the empress been here, I would not have come to this," he said.
translations.idiomatic: As death approached he told his attendants, "Had the empress still been alive, I would not have come to this."

sentences.zh: 宣華夫人陳氏，陳宣帝女也。

translations.literal: Lady Xuanhua Chen was the daughter of Emperor Xuan of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xuanhua Chen was the daughter of Emperor Xuan of Chen.

sentences.zh: 性聰慧，姿貌無雙。

translations.literal: Her nature was intelligent and clever; in looks none could pair with her.
translations.idiomatic: She was intelligent and without rival in beauty.

sentences.zh: 及陳滅，配掖庭，後選入宮為嬪。

translations.literal: When Chen perished she was assigned to the palace women; later she was chosen into the palace as consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell she was assigned to the palace women; later she was chosen as a consort.

sentences.zh: 時獨孤皇后性妒，後宮罕得進禦，唯陳氏有寵。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dugu was jealous; within the rear palace few could approach the emperor — only Chen had favor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Dugu was fiercely jealous; few women in the rear palace could approach the emperor — only Lady Chen had favor.

sentences.zh: 煬帝之在籓也，陰有奪宗之計，規為內助，每致禮焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was in his princedom he secretly had a plan to seize the succession and schemed for inner support; he often sent gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang was still a prince he secretly plotted to seize the succession and sought allies within the palace, sending gifts often.

sentences.zh: 進金蛇、金駝等物，以取媚于陳氏。

translations.literal: He presented golden snakes, golden camels, and other objects to win Chen's favor.
translations.idiomatic: He presented golden snakes, golden camels, and other curios to win her favor.

sentences.zh: 皇太子廢立之際，頗有力焉。

translations.literal: At the time of the crown prince's deposition and establishment he had considerable force.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was deposed and another installed, she had considerable influence.

sentences.zh: 及文獻皇后崩，進位為貴人。

translations.literal: When Empress Dugu the Literary died she was advanced to noble lady.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Dugu died she was promoted to noble lady.

sentences.zh: 專房擅寵，主斷內事，六宮莫與為比。

translations.literal: She monopolized the chambers and favor; she decided inner affairs — within the six palaces none could compare.
translations.idiomatic: She held exclusive favor and controlled inner affairs — none in the six palaces could compare.

sentences.zh: 及帝大漸，遺詔拜為宣華夫人。

translations.literal: When the emperor approached death the testamentary edict invested her as Lady Xuanhua.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was dying his final edict invested her as Lady Xuanhua.

sentences.zh: 初，帝寢疾于仁壽宮，夫人與皇太子同侍疾。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor was ill at Renshou Palace; the lady and the crown prince together attended his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor fell ill at Renshou Palace, Lady Chen and the crown prince attended him together.

sentences.zh: 平旦更衣，為太子所逼，夫人拒之得免。

translations.literal: At dawn when changing clothes the crown prince forced her; the lady resisted and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, while she was changing clothes, the crown prince forced himself on her; she resisted and escaped.

sentences.zh: 歸於上所，上怪其神色有異，問之。

translations.literal: She returned to the emperor's side; the emperor wondered at her changed expression and asked.
translations.idiomatic: She returned to the emperor's bedside; he noticed her altered expression and asked what had happened.

sentences.zh: 夫人泣以實對。

translations.literal: The lady wept and told the truth.
translations.idiomatic: She wept and told him the truth.

sentences.zh: 帝恚曰：「畜生何堪付大事，獨孤誠誤我！

translations.literal: The emperor in rage said: "This beast — how can he be entrusted with great affairs; Dugu truly misled me!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged, "That beast — how can he be entrusted with the realm! Dugu truly misled me!

sentences.zh: 」意謂獻皇后也。

translations.literal: " He meant the Literary Empress.
translations.idiomatic: " He meant Empress Dugu.

sentences.zh: 因呼兵部尚書柳述、黃門侍郎元岩曰：「呼我兒！

translations.literal: He then called Minister of War Liu Shu and Attendant-in-ordinary Yuan Yan and said: "Summon my son!
translations.idiomatic: He then called the Minister of War Liu Shu and the attendant-in-ordinary Yuan Yan and said, "Summon my son!

sentences.zh: 」述等呼太子。

translations.literal: " Shu and the rest called the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: " They called for the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「勇也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yong.

sentences.zh: 」述、岩出閣為敕書訖，示左僕射楊素。

translations.literal: " Shu and Yan left the gate; when the edict document was finished they showed it to Left Pushe Yang Su.
translations.idiomatic: " Shu and Yan left the gate; when the edict was drafted they showed it to the Left Pushe Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 素以白太子，太子遣張衡入寢殿，遂令夫人及後宮同侍疾者並就別室。

translations.literal: Su reported to the crown prince; the crown prince sent Zhang Heng into the sleeping hall and then ordered the lady and all in the rear palace attending illness to go to separate chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Su informed the crown prince, who sent Zhang Heng into the sleeping hall and had Lady Chen and all the women attending the sick removed to other chambers.

sentences.zh: 俄聞上崩，而未發喪也。

translations.literal: Soon they heard the emperor had died, yet mourning was not yet proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that the emperor had died, but the mourning had not yet been announced.

sentences.zh: 夫人與諸後宮相顧曰：「事變矣！

translations.literal: The lady and the women of the rear palace looked at each other and said: "Affairs have changed!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen and the palace women looked at one another and said, "Everything has changed!

sentences.zh: 」皆色動股粟。

translations.literal: " All their colors moved and their legs trembled.
translations.idiomatic: " Their faces went pale and their legs shook.

sentences.zh: 晡後，太子遣使者齎金合，帖紙於際，親署封字，以賜夫人。

translations.literal: In the afternoon the crown prince sent an envoy bearing a gold casket; paper was pasted on the seam; he personally wrote the seal character on the closure and bestowed it on the lady.
translations.idiomatic: That afternoon the crown prince sent an envoy with a gold casket, sealed at the edge in his own hand, and gave it to Lady Chen.

sentences.zh: 夫人見，怕懼，以為鴆毒，不敢發。

translations.literal: The lady saw it and was afraid, thinking it poison; she did not dare open it.
translations.idiomatic: She was terrified, thinking it held poison, and dared not open it.

sentences.zh: 使者促之，乃發，見合中有同心結數枚。

translations.literal: The envoy urged her; only then did she open it and see within the casket several knotted cords of one heart.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy pressed her; at last she opened it and found several lover's knots inside.

sentences.zh: 諸宮人相謂曰：「得免死矣！

translations.literal: The palace women said to each other: "We are spared death!
translations.idiomatic: The palace women said to one another, "We are spared!

sentences.zh: 」陳氏恚而卻坐，不肯致謝。

translations.literal: " Chen in anger sat back and would not bow in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Chen, furious, sat back and refused to thank the envoy.

sentences.zh: 諸宮人共逼之，乃拜使者。

translations.literal: The palace women together pressed her; only then did she bow to the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The other women pressed her until she bowed to the envoy.

sentences.zh: 其夜，太子蒸焉。

translations.literal: That night, the crown prince violated her.
translations.idiomatic: That night, the crown prince took her by force.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，出居仙都宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, she was moved out to Xiandu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Yang took the throne, she was moved out to Xiandu Palace.

sentences.zh: 尋召入，歲餘而終，時年二十九。

translations.literal: Soon she was summoned back in; after more than a year she died, aged twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she was summoned back in; after more than a year she died, aged twenty-nine, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 帝深悼之，為制《神傷賦》。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned her deeply and composed the "Fu on Spirit Wounded."
translations.idiomatic: the Son of Heaven mourned her deeply and composed the "Fu on Spirit Wounded."

sentences.zh: 容華夫人蔡氏，丹陽人也。

translations.literal: Lady Ronghua Cai, a native of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ronghua Cai, a native of Danyang, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 陳滅。

translations.literal: When Chen fell.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell.

sentences.zh: 以選入宮，為世婦。

translations.literal: Selected into the palace, she became a world wife.
translations.idiomatic: Selected into the palace, she became a world wife, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 容儀婉嬈，帝甚悅之。

translations.literal: Graceful and charming in bearing—the emperor greatly favored her.
translations.idiomatic: Graceful and charming in bearing—the Son of Heaven greatly favored her.

sentences.zh: 以文獻後故，希得進幸。

translations.literal: Because of Empress Wenxian, she rarely gained the emperor's bed.
translations.idiomatic: As of empress Wenxian, she rarely gained the Son of Heaven's bed.

sentences.zh: 後崩後，漸見寵遇，拜為貴人，參斷宮掖，亞于陳氏。

translations.literal: After the empress died, favor gradually increased; she was made a guiren, shared in palace decisions, second only to Lady Chen.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress died, her favor grew; she was made guiren, shared palace affairs, and ranked below Lady Chen alone.

sentences.zh: 帝寢疾，加號容華夫人。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell gravely ill, she was advanced to Lady Ronghua.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Son of Heaven fell gravely ill, she was advanced to Lady Ronghua.

sentences.zh: 帝崩後，亦為煬帝所蒸。

translations.literal: After the emperor died, she too was violated by Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: After the Son of Heaven died, she too was violated by Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 煬帝湣皇后蕭氏，梁明帝巋之女也。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang's Min Empress Xiao was daughter of Liang Mingdi Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang's Min empress Xiao was daughter of Liang Mingdi Kui.

sentences.zh: 江南風俗，二月生子者不舉。

translations.literal: In Jiangnan custom, children born in the second month were not raised.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangnan custom, children born in the second month were not raised, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 後以二月生，由是季父岌收養之。

translations.literal: Because she was born in the second month, her younger uncle Ji therefore took her to raise.
translations.idiomatic: As she was born in the second month, her younger uncle Ji therefore took her to raise.

sentences.zh: 未歲，岌夫妻俱死，轉養舅張軻家。

translations.literal: Within the year Ji and his wife both died; she was transferred to her uncle Zhang Ke's household.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year Ji and his wife both died; she was transferred to her uncle Zhang Ke's household, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 軻甚貧窶，後躬親勞苦。

translations.literal: Ke was very poor and mean; the empress herself toiled at labor.
translations.idiomatic: Ke was very poor and mean; the empress herself toiled at labor, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 煬帝為晉王，文帝為選妃于梁，卜諸女皆不吉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was Prince of Jin, Emperor Wenxian was choosing a consort for him from Liang; divination of all the daughters came up inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guang was Prince of Jin, Wenxian chose a bride from Liang; every other daughter's omen came back ill-fated.

sentences.zh: 巋乃迎後於舅氏，令使者占之，曰：「吉。

translations.literal: Kui therefore brought the empress from her uncle's house and had the envoy divine for her, saying, "Auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Kui therefore brought the empress from her uncle's house and had the envoy divine for her, saying, "Auspicious, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 」遂冊為妃。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she was invested princess consort.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon she was invested princess consort, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 後性婉順，有智識，好學解屬文，頗知占候，文帝大善之。

translations.literal: The empress by nature was gentle and compliant, had wisdom and insight, loved learning and could compose prose, and knew something of divination; Emperor Wenxian greatly approved her.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and compliant by nature, she was clever, loved books, could write, and knew some divination—Wenxian thought highly of her.

sentences.zh: 煬帝甚寵敬焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang greatly favored and respected her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang greatly favored and respected her, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 及帝嗣位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, she was established empress.
translations.idiomatic: Once he succeeded to the throne, she was established empress.

sentences.zh: 帝每遊幸，未嘗不隨從。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went on progress, she never failed to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Son of Heaven went on progress, she never failed to follow.

sentences.zh: 時後見帝失德，心知不可，不敢措言，因為《述志賦》以自寄焉。

translations.literal: At that time the empress saw the emperor's loss of virtue, knew in her heart it could not be remedied, and dared not speak—so she composed the "Fu on Expressing One's Aspirations" to lodge her feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor's virtue fail beyond repair, she dared not speak out and wrote a Fu on Expressing One's Aspirations to hold her grief.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：

translations.literal: Its text runs:
translations.idiomatic: Its text runs:

sentences.zh: 承積善之余慶，備箕帚於皇庭。

translations.literal: I share the lingering blessing of gathered good, and take up broom and dustpan in the royal court.
translations.idiomatic: I inherit the store of my family's goodness and take my humble place in the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 恐修名之不立，將負累於先靈。

translations.literal: I fear a fair name may never stand, and burden the spirits of those before me.
translations.idiomatic: I fear my name will never stand firm and will shame the spirits of my ancestors.

sentences.zh: 乃夙夜而匪懈，實夤懼于玄冥。

translations.literal: So night and day I never slacken, in true dread of the dark heavens.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night I never slacken, in honest dread of Heaven above.

sentences.zh: 雖自強而不息，亮愚蒙之多滯。

translations.literal: Though I strive on without resting, alas, dull obscurity still holds me fast.
translations.idiomatic: Though I strive without rest, dull obscurity still holds me fast.

sentences.zh: 思竭節於天衢，才追心而弗逮。

translations.literal: I would spend my loyalty on the heavenly way, but talent lags behind the heart and cannot catch it.
translations.idiomatic: I would give my loyalty on the heavenly road, but talent trails the heart and cannot keep pace.

sentences.zh: 實庸薄之多幸，荷隆寵之嘉惠。

translations.literal: How base and slight am I, yet how richly favored—I bear your lofty grace and kindly boon.
translations.idiomatic: How slight I am, yet how richly favored—I bear your grace and kindness.

sentences.zh: 賴天高而地厚，屬王道之升平。

translations.literal: Relying on heaven's height and earth's breadth, I live beneath the kingly path in ascending peace.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is high, earth is broad; I live under a kingly peace that rises.

sentences.zh: 均二儀之覆載，與日月而齊明。

translations.literal: The two poles spread their cover alike; I share the sun and moon in equal brightness.
translations.idiomatic: The two poles cover all alike; I share the sun and moon in brightness.

sentences.zh: 乃春生而夏長，等品物而同榮。

translations.literal: As spring gives birth and summer lengthens, all things arise in the same glory.
translations.idiomatic: Spring begets and summer lengthens; all things rise in one splendor.

sentences.zh: 願立志於恭儉，私自兢於誡盈。

translations.literal: I would set my will on reverence and thrift, and privately guard against fullness.
translations.idiomatic: I set my will on reverence and thrift and guard against fullness.

sentences.zh: 孰有念于知足，苟無希於濫名。

translations.literal: Who keeps the thought of enough, and does not covet a swollen name?
translations.idiomatic: Who keeps the thought of enough and does not chase swollen fame?

sentences.zh: 惟至德之弘深，情弗邇於聲色。

translations.literal: Only utmost virtue runs wide and deep—feelings do not draw near to sound and color.
translations.idiomatic: Only deepest virtue runs wide; feeling does not cling to sound and color.

sentences.zh: 感懷舊之餘恩，求故劍於宸極。

translations.literal: Moved by kindness of days gone by, I seek the old sword at the imperial pole.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by kindness of old days, I seek the old sword at the imperial pole.

sentences.zh: 叨不世之殊眄，謬非才而奉職。

translations.literal: Favored beyond this age's measure, unworthy by any reckoning I hold my post.
translations.idiomatic: Favored beyond this age's measure—unworthy, I still hold my post.

sentences.zh: 何寵祿之逾分，撫胸襟而未識。

translations.literal: How can favor and salary exceed my portion?—I press my breast and still know nothing sure.
translations.idiomatic: How can favor and salary exceed my share? I press my breast and still am unsure.

sentences.zh: 雖沐浴於恩光，內慚惶而累息。

translations.literal: Though bathed in gracious light, within I blush and tremble, breath piled upon breath.
translations.idiomatic: Bathed in gracious light, within I blush and tremble, breath on breath.

sentences.zh: 顧微躬之寡昧，思令淑之良難。

translations.literal: Looking back on this slight frame's dimness, I think how hard a good woman's path must be.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back on my slight frame, I see how hard the good woman's path is.

sentences.zh: 實不遑於啟處，將有情而自安！

translations.literal: I truly have no leisure for rest or rising—what mood can bring the heart its ease?
translations.idiomatic: I have no leisure for rest or rising—what ease can the heart find?

sentences.zh: 若臨深而履薄，心戰粟其如寒。

translations.literal: Like treading depth while walking thin ice—the heart shudders as if struck by cold.
translations.idiomatic: Like walking thin ice over deep water—the heart shudders as if struck by cold.

sentences.zh: 夫居高而必危，每處滿而防溢。

translations.literal: To stand high is ever to stand in danger; when full, ever guard against the spill.
translations.idiomatic: To stand high is to stand in danger; when full, guard against the spill.

sentences.zh: 知恣誇之非道，乃攝生於沖謐。

translations.literal: Knowing boast and excess are not the way, I gather life in quiet depth.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing boast and excess are not the way, I gather life in quiet depth, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 嗟寵辱之易驚，尚無為而抱一。

translations.literal: Alas, how soon favor and shame startle—better to hold to stillness and keep to one.
translations.idiomatic: Favor and shame startle so soon—better to hold stillness and keep to one.

sentences.zh: 履謙光而守志，且願守乎容膝。

translations.literal: I walk in modest light and guard my aim, wishing only to dwell where knees fit the room.
translations.idiomatic: I walk in modest light, guard my aim, and wish only a room that fits my knees.

sentences.zh: 珠簾玉箔之奇，金屋瑤台之美；

translations.literal: The marvel of pearl curtains and jade valance, the beauty of golden chambers and jasper terraces—
translations.idiomatic: Pearl curtains, jade valance, golden chambers, jasper terraces—

sentences.zh: 雖時俗之崇麗，蓋哲人之所鄙。

translations.literal: though the age honors such splendor, yet a sage despises it.
translations.idiomatic: the age honors such splendor, yet the sage despises it.

sentences.zh: 愧絺綌之不工，豈絲竹而喧耳。

translations.literal: Ashamed that my hempen summer dress is coarse, how could I let silk and bamboo deafen the ear?
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed my hemp dress is coarse—how could I let silk and bamboo deafen the ear?

sentences.zh: 知道德之可尊，明善惡之由己。

translations.literal: I know that moral power deserves respect, and that good and evil spring from oneself.
translations.idiomatic: I know moral power deserves respect; good and evil spring from oneself.

sentences.zh: 蕩囂煩之俗慮，乃伏膺于經史。

translations.literal: I shake off vulgar cares and clutter, and bow my heart to the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: I shake off vulgar cares and bow my heart to the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 綜箴誡以訓心，觀女圖而作軌。

translations.literal: I weave admonitions to train the heart, and study women's pictures for a model.
translations.idiomatic: I weave admonitions to train the heart and study women's pictures for a model.

sentences.zh: 遵古賢之令范，冀福祿之能綏。

translations.literal: I follow the worthy patterns of ancient sages, hoping blessings may be stilled at peace.
translations.idiomatic: I follow ancient sages' patterns, hoping blessings may rest in peace.

sentences.zh: 時循躬而三省，覺今是而昨非。

translations.literal: From time to time I turn upon myself in threefold reflection, and know today right where yesterday was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: I turn upon myself in threefold reflection and know today right where yesterday was wrong.

sentences.zh: 嗤黃、老之損思，信為善之可歸。

translations.literal: I scoff at Yellow and Lao for hampering thought; I trust that doing good may lead one home.
translations.idiomatic: I scoff at Yellow and Lao for hampering thought and trust that doing good leads home.

sentences.zh: 慕周姒之遺風，美虞妃之聖則。

translations.literal: I admire the legacy wind of the Zhou queen, and praise the holy measure of Yu's consort.
translations.idiomatic: I admire the Zhou queen's legacy wind and praise Yu's consort as holy measure.

sentences.zh: 仰先哲之高才，慕至人之休德。

translations.literal: I look up to the lofty gifts of sages past, and prize the blessed virtue of the utmost man.
translations.idiomatic: I look up to sages' lofty gifts and prize the utmost man's blessed virtue.

sentences.zh: 質非薄而難蹤，心恬愉而去惑。

translations.literal: My substance is thin and hard to trace, yet the heart, calm and pleased, casts off confusion.
translations.idiomatic: My substance is thin and hard to trace, yet a calm heart casts off confusion.

sentences.zh: 乃平生之耿介，實禮義之所遵。

translations.literal: Thus my lifelong uprightness—truly the observance ritual and right demand.
translations.idiomatic: Thus my lifelong uprightness—truly what ritual and right demand.

sentences.zh: 雖生知之不敏，庶積行以成仁。

translations.literal: Though born knowing is not quick within me, perchance heaped conduct may shape humanity.
translations.idiomatic: Though born knowing is slow in me, heaped conduct may yet shape humanity.

sentences.zh: 懼達人之蓋寡，謂何求而自陳。

translations.literal: I fear the great-minded are few indeed—what is there to seek that I should speak for myself?
translations.idiomatic: I fear the great-minded are few—what is there to seek that I should speak for myself?

sentences.zh: 誠素志之難寫，同絕筆於獲麟。

translations.literal: My plain resolve is hard to write—like laying down the brush when the unicorn was taken.
translations.idiomatic: My plain resolve is hard to write—yet like laying down the brush when the unicorn was taken.

sentences.zh: 及帝幸江都，臣下離貳，有宮人白後曰：「外聞人人欲反。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Jiangdu and retainers wavered in loyalty, a palace woman told the empress, "Outside one hears that everyone wishes to rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Once the Son of Heaven reached Jiangdu and retainers wavered in loyalty, a palace woman told the empress, "Outside one hears that everyone wishes to rebel."

sentences.zh: 」後曰：「任汝奏之。

translations.literal: The empress said, "Report it as you will."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "Report it as you will.", as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 」宮人言於帝，帝大怒曰：「非汝宜言！

translations.literal: The palace woman told the emperor; the emperor was furious and said, "That is not for you to say!"
translations.idiomatic: The palace woman told the Son of Heaven; the Son of Heaven was furious and said, "That is not for you to say!"

sentences.zh: 」乃斬之。

translations.literal: He had her beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He had her beheaded.

sentences.zh: 後宮人復白後曰：「宿衛者往往偶語謀反。

translations.literal: Palace women again told the empress, "Among the night guards many whisper in pairs, plotting rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Palace women again told the empress, "Among the night guards many whisper in pairs, plotting rebellion.", as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 」後曰：「天下事一朝至此，勢去已然，無可救也。

translations.literal: The empress said, "The realm's affairs have come in a day to this—power is gone and the form settled; nothing can save it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "The realm's affairs have come in a day to this—yet power is gone and the form settled; nothing can save it.

sentences.zh: 何用言，徒令帝憂煩耳！

translations.literal: What use in speaking?—you would only add worry and vexation to the emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: What use in speaking?—you would only add worry and vexation to the Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 」自是無復言者。

translations.literal: From then on none spoke again.
translations.idiomatic: From then on none spoke again, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 及宇文化及之亂，隨軍至聊城。

translations.literal: At the turmoil of Yuwen Huaji, she followed the army to Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the turmoil of Yuwen Huaji, she followed the army to Liaocheng, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 化及敗，沒于竇建德。

translations.literal: When Huaji was defeated, she fell into the hands of Dou Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huaji was defeated, she fell into the hands of Dou Jiande.

sentences.zh: 建德妻曹氏妒悍，煬帝妃嬪美人並使出家，並後置於武強縣。

translations.literal: Jiande's wife Lady Cao was jealous and fierce; Emperor Yang's consorts and palace beauties were all made to leave household life, and the empress was placed in Wuqiang county.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande's wife Lady Cao was jealous and fierce; Emperor Yang's consorts and palace beauties were all made to leave household life; the empress was placed in Wuqiang county.

sentences.zh: 是時突厥處羅可汗方盛，其可賀敦即隋義城公主也，遣使迎後。

translations.literal: At that time the Tujue khan Chuluo was at his height; his great empress was none other than the Sui Princess of Yicheng, who sent envoys to receive the empress.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Tujue khan Chuluo was at his height; his great empress was none other than the Sui Princess of Yicheng, who sent envoys to receive the empress, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 建德不敢留，遂攜其孫正道及諸女入於虜庭。

translations.literal: Jiande dared not detain her; he then led his grandson Zhengdao and all his daughters into the barbarians' court.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande dared not detain her; he then led his grandson Zhengdao and all his daughters into the barbarians' court, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 大唐貞觀四年，破突厥，皆以禮致之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan of Great Tang, the Turks were broken and all were brought in by ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan of Great Tang, the Turks were broken and all were brought in by ceremony, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 歸於京師，賜宅於興道里。

translations.literal: She returned to the capital and was given a residence in Xingdao Lane.
translations.idiomatic: She returned to the capital and was given a residence in Xingdao Lane, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，殂。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year she died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year she died, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 詔以皇后禮于揚州合葬於煬帝陵，諡曰湣。

translations.literal: An edict buried her with empress rites at Yangzhou, interred with Emperor Yang's tomb, posthumous title Min.
translations.idiomatic: An edict buried her with empress rites at Yangzhou, interred with Emperor Yang's tomb, posthumous title Min, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 論曰：男女正位，人倫大綱。

translations.literal: Appraisal says: Correct position of man and woman is the great bond of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal says: Correct position of man and woman is the great bond of human relations, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 三代已還，逮于漢、晉，何嘗不敗於嬌詖而興於聖淑。

translations.literal: From the Three Dynasties onward down to Han and Jin—when was there not ruin through favor and jealousy, and rise through sage and worthy women?
translations.idiomatic: From the Three Dynasties onward down to Han and Jin—yet when was there not ruin through favor and jealousy; rise through sage and worthy women?

sentences.zh: 至如後稷稟靈巨跡，神元生自天女，克昌來葉，異世同符。

translations.literal: As when Houji received spirit from a giant footprint and Shendu was born of a heavenly maid—the line flourished from afar, different ages, one sign.
translations.idiomatic: As when Houji received spirit from a giant footprint and Shendu was born of a heavenly maid—yet the line flourished from afar, different ages, one sign.

sentences.zh: 魏諸後婦人之識，無足論者。

translations.literal: The Wei empresses' women's foresight—none worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei empresses' women's foresight—yet none worth discussing.

sentences.zh: 文明邪險，幸不墜國。

translations.literal: Empress Wenming was perverse and dangerous—by good fortune the state did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: empress Wenming was perverse and dangerous—by good fortune the state did not fall.

sentences.zh: 靈後淫恣，卒亡天下。

translations.literal: Empress Ling was licentious and willful—at last she lost the realm.
translations.idiomatic: empress Ling was licentious and willful—at last she lost the realm.

sentences.zh: 傾城之誡，其在茲乎。

translations.literal: The caution of a woman who overturns states—is it not here?
translations.idiomatic: The caution of a woman who overturns states—yet is it not here?

sentences.zh: 乙後迫於畏逼，有足傷矣。

translations.literal: Empress Yi driven by terror and force—there was hurt enough indeed.
translations.idiomatic: empress Yi driven by terror and force—there was hurt enough indeed.

sentences.zh: 昔鉤弋年少子幼，漢武所以行權，魏世遂為常制，子貴而其母必死。

translations.literal: In old times, when Gouyi was young and her son still a child, Han Wu for this reason acted drastically; Wei age made it routine usage—the mother must die when the son is exalted.
translations.idiomatic: In old times, when Gouyi was young and her son still a child, Han Wu for this reason acted drastically; Wei age made it routine usage—yet the mother must die when the son is exalted.

sentences.zh: 矯枉之義，不亦過乎！

translations.literal: The righting of excess—does it not go too far!
translations.idiomatic: The righting of excess—yet does it not go too far!

sentences.zh: 孝文終革其失，良有以也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen at last reformed that fault—he had good cause.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen at last reformed that fault—yet he had good cause.

sentences.zh: 神武肇興齊業，武明追蹤周亂。

translations.literal: Shenwu first raised Qi enterprise; Wuming followed Zhou's turmoil in her track.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu first raised Qi enterprise; Wuming followed Zhou's turmoil in her track, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 溫公之敗邦家，馮妃比跡褒後。

translations.literal: Lord Wen's ruin of state and house—Consort Feng walked the trail of Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Wen's ruin of state and house—yet Consort Feng walked the trail of Bao.

sentences.zh: 然則汙隆之義，蓋有系焉。

translations.literal: Thus whether defilement or ascent has meaning—in the main it is bound together.
translations.idiomatic: Thus whether defilement or ascent has meaning—yet in the main it is bound together.

sentences.zh: 其餘作孽為眚，外平內蠹，鑒之近代，于齊為甚。

translations.literal: The rest who made calamity and scourge—outwardly calm, inwardly wasted—in recent times it was severest in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The rest who made calamity and scourge—yet outwardly calm, inwardly wasted—yet in recent times it was severest in Qi.

sentences.zh: 周氏粵自文皇，逮乎武帝，年逾二紀，世曆四君。

translations.literal: Zhou lineage from Emperor Wen down to Emperor Wu—years over two reigns, the age passed four lords.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou lineage from Emperor Wen down to Emperor Wu—yet years over two reigns, the age passed four lords.

sentences.zh: 業非草昧之辰，事殊權宜之日。

translations.literal: Enterprise was not the time of founding by the knife; affairs differed from days of expedient measure.
translations.idiomatic: Enterprise was not the time of founding by the knife; affairs differed from days of expedient measure, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 乃棄同即異，以夷亂華。

translations.literal: Yet they cast aside kin and took alien ways, using barbarians to disorder the Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they cast aside kin and took alien ways, using barbarians to disorder the Chinese, as the text has it.

sentences.zh: 汨婚姻之彝序，求豺狼之外利。

translations.literal: They fouled the ritual order of marriage and sought gain beyond the wolf's pack.
translations.idiomatic: They fouled marriage's ritual order and sought profit even from wolves.

sentences.zh: 既而報者倦矣，施者無厭。

translations.literal: Soon the requited grew weary; the granters knew no satiety.
translations.idiomatic: Soon those who had been rewarded grew weary; those who gave knew no limit.

sentences.zh: 向之所謂和親，未幾已成仇敵。

translations.literal: What had been called harmony marriage—in no time it had become foe.
translations.idiomatic: What had been called marriage for harmony—in no time had turned to enmity.

sentences.zh: 奇正之道，有異於斯。

translations.literal: The way of orthodox and unorthodox differs from this.
translations.idiomatic: The way of orthodox and unorthodox differs from this.

sentences.zh: 于時武皇雖受制於人，未親庶政，而謀士韞奇，直臣鉗口，過矣哉！

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wu, though controlled by others and not himself attending to ordinary government, yet to have planners hoarding stratagems while straight ministers had their mouths clamped—excess indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperor Wu, though others held him and he did not govern daily affairs, still had schemers hoard plans while upright ministers were silenced—how excessive!

sentences.zh: 而曆觀前載，以外戚而居宰輔者多矣；

translations.literal: Yet reading through former records, kin by marriage holding the seat of chief minister are many;
translations.idiomatic: Yet in former records, maternal kin as chief ministers are many;

sentences.zh: 而傾漢室者王族，喪周家者楊氏，何滅亡之禍，若合契焉。

translations.literal: but those who overturned Han's house were the Wang clan, those who doomed Zhou's house were the Yang—why do the woes of perishing match as if by tally?
translations.idiomatic: yet Wang's clan overturned Han, Yang's house doomed Zhou—why do ruinous fates align like tally marks?

sentences.zh: 隋文取鑒於已遠，大革前失，故母后之家不罹禍故。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen took warning from afar and greatly reformed earlier faults, so empress families did not meet disaster's cause.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi took warning from the distant past and greatly reformed old abuses, so empress families escaped ruin.

sentences.zh: 獨孤權無呂、霍，獲全仁壽之前；

translations.literal: Dugu held power but not like Lü and Huo—preserved intact before Renshou;
translations.idiomatic: Dugu held power but not like Lü and Huo—she remained whole before Renshou;

sentences.zh: 蕭氏勢異梁、竇，不傾大業之後。

translations.literal: Xiao's power unlike Liang and Dou—did not topple the great enterprise afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao's power was not like Liang and Dou—she did not topple the great enterprise after.

sentences.zh: 至或不隕舊基，或更隆克構，豈非處之以道，其所致然乎？

translations.literal: Some did not fall from the old foundation, some even further exalted what was firmly built—is it not because they were placed by the Way that this came about?
translations.idiomatic: Some did not fall from the old base, some even raised what was firmly built—is it not because they were governed by the Way?
